items.title: Algebraic cycles and the cycle group of a scheme of finite type over a field
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]], [[def-scheme-over-base]]). An **algebraic cycle** on $X$ is a formal $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of integral closed subschemes of $X$ ([[def-integral-scheme]], [[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]); it is **finite** when the combination is finite. For an integer $d$, the **group of $d$-cycles** is the free abelian group
$$Z_d(X):=\bigoplus_{V} \mathbb Z\cdot[V],$$
the direct sum running over the integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq X$ of dimension $d$ ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]], [[def-noetherian-topological-space]], [[def-free-abelian-group]]); one writes $Z_*(X)=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}Z_d(X)$. The **support** $|\alpha|$ of a cycle $\alpha=\sum_i n_i[V_i]$ is the union of the $V_i$ with $n_i\ne0$, a closed subset of $X$; a cycle is **effective** if all $n_i\ge0$.

**Conventions.** (i) A cycle class may be represented by a locally finite sum in the situations below; finite sums suffice for the schemes of finite type over a field used in this pair. (ii) All integral closed subschemes are taken with the reduced structure, and $[V]$ denotes the associated basis element; the fundamental cycle of an integral $X$ of dimension $n$ is $[X]\in Z_n(X)$. (iii) For $X$ equidimensional of pure dimension $n$ one writes $A^p(X):=A_{n-p}(X)$ for the codimension-$p$ Chow group once $A_*$ is available (def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence). (iv) No choice is used in this definition beyond the free abelian group on the set of subvarieties ([[def-free-abelian-group]]).
items.strategy:
Definition. The only points requiring care are: the free abelian group on the set of integral closed subschemes of $X$ of dimension $d$ exists ([[def-free-abelian-group]]); the set is well defined because dimension is a property of the underlying topological space ([[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); and the support of a finite combination is closed. Compare Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.1-1.3 and Stacks 42.8 (tag 02QY ff.), whose ``cycles with support'' convention is a mild generalization; we use the classical finite-support version of Fulton, which is what the later constructions in this pair use.

items.title: The order function of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ ([[def-local-ring]], [[def-noetherian-ring]], [[def-krull-dimension-of-a-ring]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]). For a nonzero $A$-module $M$ of finite length write $\ell_A(M)$ for its length ([[def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module]]). For $0\ne r\in K$ choose $a,b\in A\setminus\{0\}$ with $r=a/b$ and set
$$\operatorname{ord}_A(r):=\ell_A(A/aA)-\ell_A(A/bA)\in\mathbb Z.$$
Then:

1. $A/aA$ and $A/bA$ have finite length, so $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ is defined; in fact a Noetherian ring of dimension $0$ has finite length, and $A/aA$ has dimension $0$ for $a\ne0$ because every prime of $A/aA$ lies over the unique maximal ideal of the one-dimensional domain $A$.
2. The value $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ does not depend on the presentation $r=a/b$: if $a/b=c/d$ with $a,b,c,d\ne0$, then $ad=bc$, and the two exact sequences $0\to A/aA\xrightarrow{\,d\,}A/adA\to A/dA\to0$ and $0\to A/cA\xrightarrow{\,b\,}A/bcA\to A/bA\to0$, together with additivity of length in short exact sequences ([[cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences]]), give $\ell(A/aA)-\ell(A/bA)=\ell(A/cA)-\ell(A/dA)$.
3. $\operatorname{ord}_A(rs)=\operatorname{ord}_A(r)+\operatorname{ord}_A(s)$ and $\operatorname{ord}_A(r^{-1})=-\operatorname{ord}_A(r)$ for $r,s\in K^*$; $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)=0$ for $r\in A^*$; $\operatorname{ord}_A(r)\ge0$ for $r\in A$, with equality if and only if $r\in A^*$.
4. If $A$ is a discrete valuation ring with normalized valuation $v_A$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), then $\operatorname{ord}_A=v_A$; if $A$ is regular of dimension one, $\operatorname{ord}_A$ is the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $A$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]]).
items.strategy:
Elementary. Finiteness of the lengths in (1): $A/aA$ is a Noetherian ring of dimension $0$, hence Artinian, hence of finite length. Claim (2) is the two exact-sequence computation displayed in the statement, using additivity of length ([[cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences]]); the maps are injective because $A$ is a domain and $b,d\ne0$. Claim (3) follows by inserting finitely many intermediate terms and using multiplicativity of lengths in towers $\ell(A/aA)=\ell(A/abA)+\ell(abA/aA)$ with $abA/aA\cong A/bA$; the sign and positivity statements follow from $\ell=0\iff$ the quotient vanishes. Claim (4) is immediate from the definitions of length and of the normalized valuation. This is the order function used in Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, A.3 and proved there for arbitrary one-dimensional Noetherian local rings via Herbrand quotients; Stacks 42.2-42.6 (Key Lemma, tag 0EAX) proves the general form. The present lemma is the special case needed to define the divisor of a rational function on an integral closed subscheme (def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence).

items.title: Grothendieck groups of coherent sheaves and of vector bundles on a scheme
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme ([[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]]). Then the category of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules is abelian ([[thm-coherent-sheaves-abelian-noetherian-scheme]], [[def-coherent-module-scheme]]), and the category of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules of locally constant rank is an exact category ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]).

1. The **Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves** $K_0(X):=K_0(\operatorname{Coh}(X))$ is the abelian group with one generator $[\mathcal F]$ for each coherent sheaf, subject to $[\mathcal F]=[\mathcal F']+[\mathcal F'']$ for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-an-essentially-small-abelian-category]]); existence of the group is the group completion of the commutative monoid modulo the exact-sequence relations.
2. The **Grothendieck group of vector bundles** $K^0(X)$ is the abelian group with one generator $[\mathcal E]$ for each finite locally free sheaf of locally constant rank, subject to $[\mathcal E]=[\mathcal E']+[\mathcal E'']$ for every exact sequence $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ of such sheaves. Tensor product makes $K^0(X)$ a commutative ring with unit $[\mathcal O_X]$ ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]], [[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]]), and makes $K_0(X)$ a $K^0(X)$-module via $[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F]:=[\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F]$, using that tensoring with a locally free sheaf is exact.
3. Every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of locally Noetherian schemes induces $f^*:K^0(Y)\to K^0(X)$ by pullback of locally free sheaves ([[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]], [[lem-dual-locally-free-and-base-change]]); flat $f$ also induces $f^*:K_0(Y)\to K_0(X)$.
4. If $f:X\to Y$ is proper, the higher direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ are coherent ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]]) and vanish for $q\gg0$ over affine opens of $Y$ ([[thm-serre-finiteness-projective-cohomology]]); the resulting pushforward $f_!:K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ is defined in def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory.
5. The natural map $K^0(X)\to K_0(X)$, $[\mathcal E]\mapsto[\mathcal E]$, is well defined and additive; it is an isomorphism when $X$ is regular (lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves).
items.strategy: Definitions together with the standard exactness properties. For (3), pullback of a locally free sheaf is locally free and pullback preserves exact sequences of locally free sheaves ([[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]]), so $f^*$ is defined; for flat $f$, pullback of a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves is exact ($-\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal O_X$ is exact when $\mathcal O_X$ is flat over $\mathcal O_Y$), so $f^*$ is defined on $K_0$. For (2), tensoring a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves with a locally free sheaf is exact, so the $K^0$-action is well defined; the ring axioms are those of the tensor product. Reference: Stacks 42.69 (Appendix B: rational equivalence and $K$-groups, tag 0AYD) and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 4-5 (the Grothendieck groups of coherent and locally free sheaves and their ring structure), and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (definitions of $K_0X$ and $K^0X$, functoriality, module structure, projection formula).

items.title: Rational equivalence and the Chow group of cycles
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. For $d\in\mathbb Z$ let $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)\subseteq Z_d(X)$ be the subgroup generated by all cycles of the form
$$(i_W)_*\operatorname{div}(r),\qquad \operatorname{div}(r)=\sum_{V\subseteq W}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)\,[V],$$
where $W\subseteq X$ is an integral closed subscheme of dimension $d+1$ ([[def-integral-scheme]]), $i_W:W\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion, $r\in k(W)^*$ is a nonzero rational function on $W$ ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]), the sum runs over the integral closed subschemes $V\subseteq W$ of dimension $d$, and $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,V}}(r)$ is the order function of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] for the one-dimensional Noetherian local domain $\mathcal O_{W,V}$ ([[def-local-ring]]). The sum is finite: a cycle on $W$ has finite support, equivalently the set of codimension-one points of $W$ at which $r$ has nonzero order is finite. The elements of $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)$ are the $d$-cycles **rationally equivalent to zero**; two cycles are **rationally equivalent** if their difference is, written $\alpha\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}\beta$. The **Chow group of $d$-cycles** is
$$A_d(X):=Z_d(X)/\operatorname{Rat}_d(X),\qquad A_*(X)=\bigoplus_{d}A_d(X).$$

**Basic facts.** (i) Rational equivalence is an equivalence relation compatible with the group structure, by definition. (ii) If $W$ is a *normal* integral closed subscheme, then $\operatorname{div}(r)$ agrees with the principal Weil divisor of $r$ computed with the divisor theory of [[def-order-codimension-one-rational-function]], [[def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-group]]; in particular for $X$ integral of dimension $n$ and normal (e.g. smooth), $A_n(X)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by $[X]$ and $A_d(X)=0$ for $d>\dim X$. (iii) For $X$ equidimensional of pure dimension $n$, set $A^p(X):=A_{n-p}(X)$; this is the codimension grading used throughout. (iv) Equivalent presentation: $\alpha\sim_{\mathrm{rat}}0$ if and only if $\alpha=\sum_i (i_{W_i})_*\operatorname{div}(r_i)$ as above; this is the "Fulton 1.6" definition with supports on closed subschemes of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ specialized, and it is Stacks' Definition 42.19.1 (tag 02RW).
items.strategy:
Definition plus consistency checks. The subgroup $\operatorname{Rat}_d(X)$ is generated by the displayed cycles, so rational equivalence is well defined once the order function is; finiteness of the support of a divisor uses that the residue field at each codimension-one point of a $d+1$-dimensional integral noetherian subscheme is nonzero and only finitely many orders are nonzero, which follows from the finiteness of the localizations of a nonzero function (Stacks Lemma 42.17.x, tag 02RT). Fact (ii) is [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]](4) applied over the normal points; for normal $W$ the local rings $\mathcal O_{W,V}$ are discrete valuation rings ([[def-order-codimension-one-rational-function]]), so the order function is the valuation and $\operatorname{div}$ is the principal divisor of [[def-principal-weil-divisor-and-class-group]]. The remaining assertions are restatements of the definition. The general reference is Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.3 (p. 10) and 1.6; Stacks 42.19.1 (tag 02RW) and Lemma 42.19.3 (tag 02RX) for the localization exact sequence used in lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space.

items.title: The cycle associated to a closed subscheme and to a coherent sheaf
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a closed subscheme ([[def-closed-immersion-schemes]]) with irreducible components $Y_1,\dots,Y_r$ and generic points $\xi_i$ ([[def-irreducible-component-scheme]], [[def-generic-point-irreducible-closed-subset]]). If $\dim Y_i=d_i$, set
$$[Y]:=\sum_{i=1}^{r}\ell_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}}\bigl(\mathcal O_{Y,\xi_i}\bigr)\,[Y_i]\in Z_*(X),$$
a finite sum, where $\ell$ is module length ([[def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module]], [[def-local-ring]]). Then:

1. $[Y]$ depends only on the closed subscheme structure of $Y$, equals $[Y]$ (the basis element) when $Y$ is integral, and $[Y]=\sum_i[Y_i]$ when $Y$ is reduced. More generally, if $\mathcal F$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]) supported on $Y$, then $[\mathcal F]:=\sum_i \ell_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}}(\mathcal F_{\xi_i})\,[Y_i]$ is a cycle, the **cycle associated to $\mathcal F$**, and $[\mathcal F]$ is additive in short exact sequences of coherent sheaves on $X$.
2. (Flat pullback of the cycle of a subscheme) If $f:X'\to X$ is flat and $Y\subseteq X$ is a closed subscheme, then $[f^{-1}(Y)]=f^*[Y]$ in the sense of lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups whenever $f^{-1}(Y)$ has pure codimension in $X'$ determined by $f$.
3. For the structure sheaf, $[Y]=[\mathcal O_Y]$ where the latter is computed with $\mathcal O_Y$ viewed as a coherent sheaf on $X$ (extension by zero, [[lem-sheaf-supported-on-a-closed-subset-is-a-pushforward]]).
4. If $Y$ is a closed subscheme of pure dimension $d$ and $D\subseteq X$ is an effective Cartier divisor with $Y\not\subseteq D$, then $[Y\cap D]=[D|_Y]$ computed in $Z_{d-1}(X)$ via the closed subscheme $Y\cap D$.
items.strategy:
Definition and standard properties. (1) is Stacks Lemma 42.9.1 (tag 02QS) and Lemma 42.9.3, together with the additivity Lemma 42.10.1 (tag 02QW); the finiteness of the sum uses that a Noetherian topological space has finitely many irreducible components (cor-noetherian-spectrum-has-finitely-many-irreducible-components). (2) is Stacks Lemma 42.14.1-42.14.3 (tag 02RA); the pure-codimension statement is the flat fibrewise dimension statement for the localized situation, thm-flat-families-fibre-dimension-locally-constant for the proper case and Stacks 42.13.1 for the general flat fibre-dimension statement. (3) is [[lem-sheaf-supported-on-a-closed-subset-is-a-pushforward]] plus the identification of local lengths. (4) expands $D|_Y$; the multiplicities agree because the local equation of $D$ is a nonzerodivisor on $\mathcal O_Y$ exactly when $Y\not\subseteq D$ for an effective Cartier divisor. Compare Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.5 and 2.3 and Vakil 245 Class 2.

items.title: Vector bundles and coherent sheaves generate the same K-classes on a regular scheme
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian scheme of finite dimension over a field, or more generally a regular Noetherian scheme with affine diagonal which is quasi-compact and of finite type over a fixed Noetherian base ([[def-locally-noetherian-and-noetherian-scheme]], [[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]). Then the natural map
$$K^0(X)\longrightarrow K_0(X),\qquad [\mathcal E]\longmapsto[\mathcal E]$$
of [[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]] is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Equivalently: every coherent sheaf on $X$ has a finite resolution by finite locally free sheaves
$$0\to\mathcal E_m\to\cdots\to\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E_0\to\mathcal F\to0,$$
so that $[\mathcal F]=\sum_{i=0}^m(-1)^i[\mathcal E_i]$, and the alternating sum is independent of the resolution. Consequently, for a smooth $k$-scheme of finite type, all of $K_0$ is generated by vector bundles, and additive invariants defined on vector bundles (such as the Chern character of def-chern-character-and-todd-class) extend to $K_0$.
items.strategy: Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 4, Theoreme 2 proves in full that on a nonsingular quasi-projective variety every coherent sheaf admits a finite locally free resolution, and deduces $K^0(X)=K_0(X)$; their proof uses the resolution of a coherent sheaf by a quotient of a locally free sheaf (their Lemme 10, using quasi-projectivity) and the devissage argument reducing to the structure sheaves of subvarieties. Stacks proves the same statement as the composite $K_0(\mathrm{Vect}(X))\to A^*(X)\to CH^*(X)$ being an isomorphism for quasi-compact regular $X$ of finite type over the base with affine diagonal and bounded dimension function (Chow Homology, Lemma 42.58.1, tag 0FEY), citing Derived Categories of Schemes Lemmas 36.8, 38.4 and 38.5 for the identification $K'_0(X)=K_0(X)=K_0(\mathrm{Vect}(X))$; its proof shows in particular that the alternating sum of a resolution gives a well-defined class. Locally, a finitely generated module over a regular local ring has finite projective dimension equal to the dimension of the ring ([[cor-regular-local-residue-field-projective-dimension-dimension]] and the Auslander-Buchsbaum formula); the global finite resolution is then produced by the devissage/patching argument (Borel-Serre 4; Vakil 245 Class 18, ``Fact'': resolution exists with the cohomological-measure sketch).

items.title: Pushforward in algebraic K-theory of coherent sheaves
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice, inherited from the coherence and finiteness suppliers below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]); then $Y$ is locally Noetherian and for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ all higher direct images $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ are coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]], [[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]]) and vanish for all sufficiently large $q$ ([[thm-serre-finiteness-projective-cohomology]] over affine opens of $Y$, the vanishing being local on $Y$). Set
$$f_![\mathcal F]:=\sum_{q\ge0}(-1)^q\,[R^qf_*\mathcal F]\in K_0(Y)$$
([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]). Then:

1. $f_!$ is a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(X)\to K_0(Y)$ of abelian groups: a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ on $X$ induces the long exact sequence of higher direct images $0\to f_*\mathcal F'\to f_*\mathcal F\to f_*\mathcal F''\to R^1f_*\mathcal F'\to\cdots$ ([[def-higher-direct-image-sheaf]], [[cor-derived-long-exact-sequence]]), whose alternating sum is zero, giving $f_![\mathcal F]=f_![\mathcal F']+f_![\mathcal F'']$.
2. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}_!=\operatorname{id}$ and $(g\circ f)_!=g_!\circ f_!$ for composable proper morphisms: the Leray spectral sequence for the composition degenerates after the alternating sum because only finitely many terms in each bidegree are nonzero ([[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]]).
3. (Compatibility with the module structure) $f_!(f^*[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F])=[\mathcal E]\cdot f_![\mathcal F]$ for $\mathcal E$ locally free on $Y$ and $\mathcal F$ coherent on $X$, i.e. the projection formula; this is proved in lem-projection-formula-in-algebraic-k-theory. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $X$ projective, $f_![\mathcal F]=\chi(X,\mathcal F)$ is the Euler characteristic ([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]).
items.strategy: Definitions and standard homological algebra, following Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 3 (the direct image of a coherent sheaf and the theorem on the coherence/finiteness of the higher direct images) and 5 (pushforward on $K$ and its functoriality), and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (definition $f_*[\mathcal F]=\sum(-1)^i[R^if_*\mathcal F]$, projection formula, functoriality). Well-definedness: the long exact sequence of higher direct images is the standard long exact sequence for a short exact sequence of complexes in the derived category; the alternating sum of its terms is zero because the sequence has finitely many nonzero terms, using the coherence and higher vanishing of the $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ ([[thm-proper-pushforward-coherent]], [[thm-serre-finiteness-projective-cohomology]]). Functoriality: the Leray spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^pg_*(R^qf_*\mathcal F)\Rightarrow R^{p+q}(g\circ f)_*\mathcal F$ ([[thm-leray-spectral-sequence-for-sheaf-cohomology]]) has finitely supported rows and columns (coherence plus the vanishing statements), so the alternating sum of $E_\infty$ equals the alternating sum of the total derived images, giving $g_!f_!= (g\circ f)_!$. Point 3 is lem-projection-formula-in-algebraic-k-theory.

items.title: Proper pushforward of cycles is well defined on Chow groups
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]). For an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq X$ with generic point $\eta$, let $W=\overline{f(V)}\subseteq Y$ with the reduced structure, an integral closed subscheme ([[def-scheme-theoretic-image]], [[thm-proper-morphism-closed-image]]). Define
$$f_*[V]:=\begin{cases} [k(V):k(W)]\cdot[W], & \dim W=\dim V,\\ 0, & \dim W<\dim V,\end{cases}$$
where $k(V)$, $k(W)$ are the function fields ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]] or [[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]]) and $[k(V):k(W)]$ is the extension degree ([[def-extension-degree-and-finite-extension]]), finite because a dominant morphism $V\to W$ of integral finite-type $k$-schemes with $\dim V=\dim W$ has algebraic, hence finite, function field extension. Extending $\mathbb Z$-linearly gives $f_*:Z_d(X)\to Z_d(Y)$ for all $d$. Then:

1. $f_*$ is a homomorphism of graded groups and $f_*(\operatorname{Rat}_d(X))\subseteq \operatorname{Rat}_d(Y)$, so it descends to $f_*:A_d(X)\to A_d(Y)$ ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).
2. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}_*=\operatorname{id}$ and $(g\circ f)_*=g_*\circ f_*$ for proper $f,g$; the degree is multiplicative in towers of finite function-field extensions.
3. (Base change) For a cartesian square with flat $g$ and proper $f$, the compatibility of lem-pushforward-pullback-compatibility-chow holds.
4. (Normalization) If $f$ is finite flat of constant degree $n$ between integral schemes of the same dimension, then $f_*[X]=n[Y]$.

Point (1) is the nontrivial assertion: for $W\subseteq X$ integral of dimension $d+1$ and $r\in k(W)^*$ one has
$$f_*\bigl(\operatorname{div}_W(r)\bigr)=\operatorname{div}_{f(W)}\bigl(N_{k(W)/k(f(W))}(r)\bigr)$$
when $\dim f(W)=\dim W$, and $f_*(\operatorname{div}_W(r))=0$ when $\dim f(W)<\dim W$; here $N$ is the field norm.
items.strategy:
Follow Stacks 42.11-42.12 (tags 02R3-02R4) for the definition and the reduction of the norm identity, and Stacks 42.18 (tag 02RS) and Lemma 42.20.3 (tag 02S0) for the well-definedness of $f_*$ on Chow groups; the displayed norm identity is Stacks Lemma 42.18.3. The key local computation is: for a codimension-one point $V$ of $W$ lying over a codimension-one point $U$ of $W'=f(W)$, the local degree $[k(V):k(U)]$ and the order functions satisfy $\operatorname{ord}_{U}(N(r))=\sum_{V\mapsto U}\operatorname{ord}_{V}(r)\,[k(V):k(U)]$, proved by reducing to the case of a one-dimensional local domain via [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] (Stacks Lemma 42.18.1-42.18.2); the sum is finite and the unramified-in-codimension-one case follows from the norm's behaviour on DVRs. Functoriality (2) is Stacks Lemma 42.12.2 and the multiplicativity of extension degrees (thm-multiplicativity-of-separable-degree for the separable part, def-inseparable-degree for the rest). Compare Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.4, and Vakil 245 Classes 2-4, where the same norm computation is written out.

items.title: Projection formula in algebraic K-theory
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over a field $k$ ([[def-proper-morphism]], [[def-locally-finite-type-and-finite-type-morphism]]). Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then for every $q\ge0$ there is a canonical isomorphism of coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules
$$R^qf_*\bigl(f^*\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\bigr)\;\cong\;\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}R^qf_*\mathcal F,$$
and consequently, in $K_0(Y)$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]),
$$f_!\bigl(f^*[\mathcal E]\cdot[\mathcal F]\bigr)=[\mathcal E]\cdot f_![\mathcal F],$$
where $f_!$ is the pushforward of [[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]] and the products are the $K$-theory module products.
items.strategy: Standard projection formula for higher direct images: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ over which $\mathcal E$ is free, the formula reduces to the case $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_Y$, where it is the naturality of $f_*$; the general case follows by additivity and local trivialization, since locally free sheaves are a direct summand locally ([[lem-internal-hom-fp-qc]] gives the internal-hom adjunction that produces the canonical map, and the trace/evaluation argument shows it is an isomorphism). See Stacks, *Cohomology of Schemes*, Section 30.6 (projection formula) for the complete proof, and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 5, c (the projection isomorphisms for the direct image functor) with Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.2 (Lemma: $f_*(f^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot f_*\beta$, proved from $R^if_*(f^*E\otimes F)=E\otimes R^if_*F$). Summing over $q$ with alternating signs gives the $K$-theory identity, since $[\mathcal E]$ acts on $K_0$ by tensor product.

items.title: K-theory of projective space and surjectivity for projections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field.

1. In $K^0(\mathbb P^n_k)=K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]], [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) the classes $[\mathcal O(i)]$, $0\le i\le n$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis; equivalently $K_0(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z^{n+1}$ generated by the twisting sheaves ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], [[thm-twisting-sheaf-invertible-standard-graded]]).
2. For every locally Noetherian $k$-scheme $Y$ and every $n\ge0$, the exterior-product map
$$K_0(Y)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K_0(\mathbb P^n_k)\longrightarrow K_0(\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY)$$
is surjective; here $K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$ is the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]) and the product is $[\mathcal F]\times[\mathcal G]\mapsto[\mathrm{pr}_1^*\mathcal F\otimes\mathrm{pr}_2^*\mathcal G]$ ([[lem-tensor-qc-modules-quasi-coherent]], [[lem-pullback-qc-module-quasi-coherent]]).
3. More generally, if $\mathcal E$ is a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module of rank $r+1$, the projective bundle $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ has $K_0(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$ generated over $K_0(Y)$ by $1,[\mathcal O(1)],\dots,[\mathcal O(r)]$, via the localization/affine-bundle computation of $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ into affine bundles over a cell decomposition of the fibres ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]]).
items.strategy: Vakil 245 Class 19 Section 1.1: the excision sequence for $K_0$, $K_0(Z)\to K_0(X)\to K_0(U)\to0$ (proved as in the Chow case, Hartshorne II.6.10(c)), together with the affine-bundle isomorphism $K_0(\mathbb A^1\times Y)\cong K_0(Y)$, applied to the cell decomposition $\mathbb P^n=\mathbb A^0\sqcup\mathbb A^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup\mathbb A^n$ gives inductively that $K_0(\mathbb P^n)$ is generated by $[\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^0}],\dots,[\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n}]$, and the twist exact sequences $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{n-1}}\to0$ express these in terms of the $[\mathcal O(i)]$, $0\le i\le n$; the same proof with $Y$ in place of a point gives (2). Independent complete treatment: Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 8 (Proposition 7: excision $K(X')\to K(X)\to K(U)\to0$; Proposition 8: $K(X)\cong K(X\times\mathbb A^1)$) and 9 (Proposition 9: $K(A)\otimes K(P)\to K(A\times P)$ surjective, proved by the same cellular induction; the Remark after Proposition 10 gives the basis $1,a,\dots,a^r$ of $K(\mathbb P^r)$ with $a=[\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}]$ and $a^{r+1}=0$). Surjectivity in (2) is the exact statement needed for thm-rr-for-projective-space-projections. The identification $K_0=K^0$ for projective space is [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]] (smooth, regular).

items.title: Flat pullback of cycles is well defined on Chow groups
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a flat morphism of schemes locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-flat-morphism-schemes]]) all of whose nonempty fibres have pure dimension $n$ ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]], [[def-dimension-noetherian-topological-space]]); for instance $f$ smooth of relative dimension $n$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]], [[lem-smooth-fibres-smooth]]) or an open immersion with $n=0$. For an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ let $f^{-1}(V)=V\times_Y X$ be the scheme-theoretic preimage and let $[f^{-1}(V)]$ be its cycle ([[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]]). Extending linearly gives $f^*:Z_d(Y)\to Z_{d+n}(X)$. Then:

1. $f^{-1}(V)$ is equidimensional of dimension $\dim V+n$, so $f^*[V]$ is a pure $(d+n)$-cycle; this is the only place the pure-fibre-dimension hypothesis is used.
2. $f^*(\operatorname{Rat}_d(Y))\subseteq\operatorname{Rat}_{d+n}(X)$: for an integral closed subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ of dimension $d+1$ and $r\in k(W)^*$, the pulled back rational function $f^*r$ on $f^{-1}(W)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}_{f^{-1}(W)}(f^*r)=f^*(\operatorname{div}_W(r))$, and the right-hand side lies in $\operatorname{Rat}_{d+n}(X)$.
3. Consequently $f^*$ descends to a graded homomorphism $f^*:A_d(Y)\to A_{d+n}(X)$ ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]]).
4. (Functoriality) $\operatorname{id}^*=\operatorname{id}$ and $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$ for composable flat morphisms of the stated kind; if $f$ is an open immersion then $f^*$ is the restriction of cycles.
5. (Localization) If $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion and $i:Z=X\setminus U\hookrightarrow X$ the complementary reduced closed subscheme, the sequence $A_*(Z)\xrightarrow{i_*}A_*(X)\xrightarrow{j^*}A_*(U)\to0$ is exact (using [[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]] for $i_*$).
items.strategy:
Follow Stacks 42.13-42.14 (tag 02RA) and Lemma 42.20.2 (tag 02RZ?) for well-definedness, and Lemma 42.19.3 (tag 02RX) for the localization sequence in (5); Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.7 for the classical statement. (1) is the flat fibre-dimension statement: for $f$ flat and locally of finite type with fibres of pure dimension $n$, the preimage of an integral closed subscheme is equidimensional of dimension $\dim V+n$ (Stacks Lemma 42.13.1-42.13.3; compare [[thm-flat-families-fibre-dimension-locally-constant]], which supplies the locally-constant fibre dimension in the proper flat case). (2) reduces fibrewise: over an affine chart with $f$ given by a flat ring map $A\to B$, the divisor of $f^*r$ is computed by the image of a principal divisor under the flat map, and multiplicities are preserved by flatness (Stacks Lemma 42.14.2). (4) is Stacks Lemma 42.14.4. The hypothesis of pure fibre dimension cannot be dropped: see cex-arbitrary-pullback-does-not-define-a-chow-operation for the failure of preimage cycles when fibre dimensions jump.

items.title: Proper pushforward and flat pullback commute in a fibre square
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc} X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\ \downarrow f' & & \downarrow f\\ Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y\end{array}$$
be a cartesian square of schemes locally of finite type over $k$ ([[def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property]]), with $f$ proper (hence $f'$ proper, [[lem-base-change-open-closed-immersions]]) and $g$ flat of relative dimension $n$ with all fibres of pure dimension $n$ (hence $g'$ flat of relative dimension $n$, [[lem-flat-morphisms-stable-base-change]]). Then the two graded homomorphisms $A_d(X)\to A_{d+n}(Y')$ agree:
$$g^*\circ f_*\;=\;f'_*\circ g'^*,$$
where $f_*,f'_*$ are proper pushforwards ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]) and $g^*,g'^*$ are flat pullbacks ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]]).
items.strategy:
Follow Stacks Lemma 42.15.1 (tag 02RF, ``push and pull''), Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, Proposition 1.7.1, and Vakil 245 Class 4 (``proper pushforward commutes with flat pullback''). Reduce to a cycle $\alpha=[V]$, $V\subseteq X$ integral. If $\dim f(V)<\dim V$ then both sides vanish. Otherwise put $W=\overline{f(V)}$ and compute both sides on the components of $V\times_W (W\times_Y Y')$ using the flatness of $g$ (the preimage of $W$ is the underlying set of $W\times_Y Y'$ with multiplicities all equal to $1$ because $g$ is flat and the local rings of $W\times_YY'$ over $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ are flat) and the multiplicativity of extension degrees in the cartesian field diagram $k(V)\otimes_{k(W)}k(W')\to k(V')$. Both sides then equal $\sum [k(V_i):k(W')]\cdot[W_i']$ over the components. The remaining assertions are the functoriality of flat pullback and the base-change stability of properness.

items.title: Intersection with an invertible sheaf and the first Chern class
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-invertible-sheaf]]).

1. **Integral case.** Let $W\subseteq X$ be integral of dimension $n$, with function field $k(W)$ ([[def-sheaf-total-quotient-rings]], [[def-field-of-fractions]]), and let $s$ be a nonzero rational section of $L|_W$ ([[def-rational-section-line-bundle]]). The **Weil divisor of $s$** is
$$\operatorname{div}_L(s)=\sum_{Z\subseteq W}\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{W,Z}}(s)[Z]\in Z_{n-1}(W),$$
the sum over the codimension-one integral closed subschemes $Z\subseteq W$, with the order function of [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]] read on a local generator of $L$ at the generic point of $Z$; the sum has finite support. The **first Chern class class** $c_1(L)\cap[W]:=[\operatorname{div}_L(s)]\in A_{n-1}(W)$ is independent of the chosen nonzero rational section (two such differ by a rational function, whose divisor is rationally equivalent to zero), and therefore defines the class $c_1(L|_W)\in A^1(W)$.
2. **General case.** For an integral closed subscheme $i:W\hookrightarrow X$ of dimension $d+1$ set $c_1(L)\cap[W]:=i_*\bigl(c_1(i^*L)\cap[W]\bigr)\in A_d(X)$, where $i_*$ is the proper pushforward ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]); extend $\mathbb Z$-linearly. The resulting operation $c_1(L)\cap-:A_{d+1}(X)\to A_d(X)$ is well defined on Chow groups (this is the content of the next two references) and graded.

**Basic properties.** (i) $c_1(L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}N)\cap\alpha=(c_1(L)+c_1(N))\cap\alpha$ and $c_1(\mathcal O_X)\cap\alpha=0$ for all $\alpha$. (ii) If $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ is a global section with $\dim Z(s)\le d$ and with $s$ a nonzerodivisor on $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ at every generic point $\xi$ of a $d$-dimensional component of $Z(s)$, then $c_1(L)\cap[Y]_{d+1}=[Z(s)]_d$; in particular, if $D\subseteq X$ is an effective Cartier divisor with $L\cong\mathcal O_X(D)$ and $s$ is the tautological section, then $c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))\cap[X]=[D]$. (iii) $c_1(L)\cap-$ commutes with proper pushforward and flat pullback: for $f:X\to Y$ proper, $f_*(c_1(f^*L)\cap\alpha)=c_1(L)\cap f_*\alpha$, and for $f$ flat of relative dimension $n$, $f^*(c_1(L)\cap\alpha)=c_1(f^*L)\cap f^*\alpha$. (iv) $c_1(L)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of $L$.
items.strategy:
Follow Stacks 42.24-42.30: the divisor associated with an invertible sheaf is Definition 42.24.1 (tag 02SJ), the section computation is Lemma 42.24.2 (tag 02SK), the intersection operation is Definition 42.25.1 (tag 02SO) with additivity Lemma 42.25.2 (tag 02SP) and the zero-scheme formula Lemma 25.4 (tag 02SQ), compatibility with flat pullback and proper pushforward is Lemma 42.26.1-42.26.3 (tag 0AYA-0EPJ), and the factoring through rational equivalence is Stacks 42.28-42.30 (the Key Lemma 42.6.3 (tag 0EAX) plus the Gysin homomorphism Lemma 42.30.1, tag 02TK); the same development is Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6 and Vakil 245 Class 6. The only subtlety in the definition is that for $[W]$ one must use a *rational* section of $L|_W$, which exists because $L|_W$ is trivial at the generic point of the integral scheme $W$; the resulting class is independent of the section by [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]](3) applied to the ratio of two sections. Property (ii) is Stacks Lemma 25.4, whose proof via Lemma 25.3 (tag 0EPI) is a length computation in the one-dimensional local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ and uses cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences.

items.title: Chow groups of projective space by cellular decomposition
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$. Then for every $d$:
$$A_d(\mathbb P^n_k)=\begin{cases}\mathbb Z\cdot[\mathbb P^d], & 0\le d\le n,\\ 0, & \text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
where $\mathbb P^d\subseteq\mathbb P^n$ is a $d$-dimensional linear subspace and $[\mathbb P^d]$ its class ([[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]], [[def-algebraic-cycle-and-cycle-group]]). In particular the degree homomorphism
$$\deg:A_0(\mathbb P^n_k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathbb Z,\qquad \sum_x m_x[x]\longmapsto\sum_x m_x[\kappa(x):k\bigr],$$
is an isomorphism; its inverse sends $1$ to $[\mathbb P^0]$ for any $k$-rational point, and every $0$-cycle whose support consists of $k$-rational points has class $(\sum_x m_x)\,[\mathbb P^0]$. For $k=\mathbb C$ this is the classical cellular decomposition. More generally, $A_*(\mathbb A^n_k)$ has $A_0(\mathbb A^n_k)=0$ and $A_d(\mathbb A^n_k)=0$ for $d>0$, since every cycle on affine space is cut down by principal divisors of linear functions (this is the $n=1$ case of [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]] transport).
items.strategy:
Induction on $n$ using the localization sequence of [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]](5) for the open immersion $j:\mathbb A^n=\mathbb P^n\setminus\mathbb P^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n$ and the closed immersion $i:\mathbb P^{n-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n$: the sequence $A_d(\mathbb P^{n-1})\xrightarrow{i_*}A_d(\mathbb P^n)\xrightarrow{j^*}A_d(\mathbb A^n)\to0$ is exact (Stacks Lemma 42.19.3, tag 02RX). If $A_*(\mathbb A^n)=0$ in positive degrees and $A_0(\mathbb A^n)=0$, then $i_*$ is surjective, and induction gives that the classes of linear subspaces generate. The affine statement: by homotopy invariance $A_*(\mathbb A^n)\cong A_*(\operatorname{Spec}k)=\mathbb Z$ placed in degree $0$ (Stacks 42.21, and [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]] for the affine-bundle surjectivity of Stacks Lemma 42.32.1, tag 02TT); alternatively use the explicit principal divisors $\operatorname{div}(x-a)$ and $\operatorname{div}(y-b)$ of the coordinate functions on the lines through a point, which kill every point and every curve class. Injectivity in the induction: $\ker i_*$ is generated by $[\mathbb P^{d-1}]$? the computation is standard (Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 1.8-1.9 and Example 1.9.3; Vakil 245 Class 11; Cela, *Intersection Theory* Lecture 4). The degree formula is the $d=0$ case read off from the presentation, with $[x]=[\kappa(x):k][\mathbb P^0]$ obtained by pushing forward a closed point along the flat pullback to the line through it.
