items.title: Localization and homotopy invariance for Chow groups
items.statement: For a closed immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with complement $u:U\hookrightarrow T$, $A_m(Z)\xrightarrow{j_*}A_m(T)\xrightarrow{u^*}A_m(U)\to0$ is exact. Projection $T\times\mathbb A^r\to T$ gives an isomorphism $A_m(T)\cong A_{m+r}(T\times\mathbb A^r)$. These statements hold for finite type schemes over a field and locally finite cycles on locally finite type schemes.
items.strategy: Source: Stacks 42.19.3, 42.32 and 42.36.3. For localization, close each integral cycle of $U$ in $T$ to prove surjectivity. If the restriction of a cycle is a sum of principal divisors, close their supporting integral subvarieties in $T$ and extend the same rational functions; their divisors restrict to the specified divisors on $U$. Subtracting them leaves a cycle supported on $Z$, proving exactness. This also proves that locally finite sums can be used. For $\mathbb A^1_T$, surjectivity of pullback is proved on each integral cycle $V$: if $V$ is the whole line over its integral image, it is a pullback; otherwise over the generic point of its image it is the divisor of a polynomial in the line coordinate, and subtracting that principal divisor leaves cycles over a smaller closed subset. Noetherian induction finishes. Pullback is injective since the Cartier Gysin for the zero section is a left inverse (on a pulled-back cycle it cuts the coordinate by a nonzerodivisor and gives its original fundamental cycle). Iterate this argument for $\mathbb A^r_T$.  For injectivity in rank $r$, compose the Cartier Gysins of the $r$ coordinate-zero divisors; each cuts the corresponding polynomial coordinate on every pulled-back integral cycle and their composition is a left inverse. This is an argument with divisor Gysin only, independent of higher-codimension Gysin or Chern classes.

items.title: Deformation to the normal cone and specialization
items.statement: For a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ with ideal $\mathcal I$, put $C_XY=\operatorname{Spec}_X(\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1})$ and $M=\operatorname{Bl}_{X\times\{\infty\}}(Y\times\mathbb P^1)$. Let $B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$ be the strict transform of $Y\times\{\infty\}$. The fibre at infinity is the sum $M_\infty=B+\mathbb P(C_XY\oplus1)$ of effective Cartier divisors, whose intersection is $\mathbb P(C_XY)$; this is a union with a common boundary, not a disjoint union. Projectivized cones here use the lines convention $\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I}\mathcal O_Y[S])$. Off infinity $M\cong Y\times\mathbb A^1$, and $D_i:=M\setminus B$ has special fibre $C_XY$ and ordinary fibres $Y$. It is flat over $\mathbb P^1$. The specialization $\sigma_i:A_m(Y)\to A_m(C_XY)$ is obtained by extending the flat pullback of a cycle to $D_i$, then taking Cartier Gysin at infinity. It sends an integral $[V]$ to the fundamental cycle $[C_{X\cap V}V]$ pushed to $C_XY$. For a regular immersion of codimension $d$, the normal cone equals the rank-$d$ normal bundle $N_{X/Y}$. The construction works for finite type schemes over a field, with locally finite cycles in the locally finite type case.
items.strategy:
Sources read: Stacks 42.53 and 42.48.1, with Vakil Class14 as a sketch comparison only. Near infinity write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and let $t$ vanish at infinity. The $t$-chart of the blowup has ring $A[t,I/t]=\sum_{n\ge0}t^{-n}I^n[t]\subset A[t,t^{-1}]$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective and its quotient is $\operatorname{gr}_I A$. In the chart of a generator $a\in I$, the ring is $A[I/a][t/a]$ (the affine blowup algebra means the subring of $A_a$, including its usual torsion removal); $t=a(t/a)$, so its fibre is the sum of the exceptional divisor $a=0$ and the strict transform $t/a=0$. The strict transform charts are exactly $\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and its intersection with the exceptional divisor is $\operatorname{Proj}\operatorname{gr}_I A$. This proves the fibre and open-chart assertions, even for singular $Y$. The charts embed in $A[t,t^{-1}]$ or are polynomial rings over the affine blowup algebras, and are torsion-free as $k[t]$-modules; all nonzero polynomials act injectively. A torsion-free module over the PID $k[t]$ is flat (every finitely generated submodule is free and the module is their filtered union). The infinity charts and ordinary product charts thus prove flatness without assuming $Y$ integral or misidentifying the centre as Cartier.
Localization gives a lift of the pulled-back class to $D_i$; two lifts differ by a class supported on $C_XY$. Cartier Gysin kills this difference because the normal line to the infinity fibre is trivial: $j^!j_*\gamma=c_1(1)\gamma=0$. Thus specialization is well defined on Chow classes. On $[V]$, closure in the $t$-chart is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_V[t,I\mathcal O_V/t]$; cutting by $t$ produces $\operatorname{gr}_{I\mathcal O_V}\mathcal O_V$, giving the asserted cone cycle with its generic lengths. For a regular sequence, the monomials in its generators identify $\operatorname{gr}_I A$ with $\operatorname{Sym}_{A/I}(I/I^2)$, hence the cone is $N_{X/Y}$.

items.title: The projective bundle formula for Chow groups
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$, and let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank $r\ge1$ ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Let
$$\pi:\mathbb P(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{Proj}_X\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\longrightarrow X$$
be the projective bundle in the quotient convention, with tautological quotient $\pi^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(\mathcal E)}(1)$ ([[def-projective-bundle-scheme]], [[def-relative-proj-quasi-coherent-graded-algebra]], [[thm-projective-bundle-represents-line-quotients]]), and put $\xi:=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ ([[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]); $\pi$ is smooth of relative dimension $r-1$ ([[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]), so flat pullback $\pi^*$ is defined ([[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]], [[lem-smooth-fibres-smooth]]). Then for every $d\in\mathbb Z$ the map
$$\bigoplus_{i=0}^{r-1}A_{d+i}(X)\longrightarrow A_{d+r-1}\bigl(\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\bigr),\qquad (\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_{r-1})\longmapsto\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}\xi^i\cap\pi^*\alpha_i,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups. More precisely, $\pi_*(\xi^s\cap\pi^*\alpha)=0$ for $s<r-1$ and $\pi_*(\xi^{r-1}\cap\pi^*\alpha)=\alpha$ for all $\alpha\in A_*(X)$ ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]).

No smoothness of $X$ is assumed; if $X$ is smooth equidimensional of dimension $n$ then $\mathbb P(\mathcal E)$ is smooth equidimensional and the formula is a statement about the codimension-graded Chow groups $A^*(X)$, $A^*(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$.
items.strategy: Stacks42.36.1-36.2, full proofs read. For $\alpha=[V]$, choose $r-1$ independent sections in a trivialization over its generic point: successive hyperplanes leave a section, whose pushforward is $[V]$. Each smaller hyperplane power has positive-dimensional fibres and pushes to zero. Any difference from choosing the generic trivialization is supported on a smaller closed subset, and induction plus the $c_1$ projection formula proves these identities globally. For injectivity of the displayed map push down to get $\alpha_{r-1}=0$, then multiply by $\xi$ and push to get $\alpha_{r-2}=0$, continuing down to $\alpha_0$. For surjectivity, reduce to integral $X$ by pushforward from its components. Trivialize $E$ on a dense open $U$. For $U\times\mathbb P^{r-1}$, stratify projective space into affine spaces; localization and affine homotopy invariance give generators $[\mathbb P^j]$ pulled from classes of $U$. Each generator is a hyperplane power times $\pi^*$ by repeated Cartier cutting, so the displayed map is surjective over $U$. Lift its coefficients to $X$ by localization. The residual class is supported over $X\setminus U$; induction on the dimension of the integral image proves surjectivity there, and push-pull brings it to $X$. This argument is valid without a Chow ring on $X$: $\xi$ is a first Chern cap operator and the displayed direct-sum map is an isomorphism of groups, not a module over an undefined ring.

items.title: Bivariant Chow operations
items.statement: For $f:Z\to T$, a degree-$d$ bivariant Chow operation assigns to every locally finite type $T'\to T$ homomorphisms $c:A_m(T')\to A_{m-d}(Z\times_TT')$, commuting with proper pushforward, flat pullback of fixed relative dimension, and Cartier divisor Gysin. Restriction along any base morphism, composition, and proper pushforward of such operations are defined by their action. Flat pullback and proper pushforward give bivariant operations, as does Cartier divisor Gysin. Equality can be tested on fundamental classes of integral schemes over $T$; it suffices to test after a proper birational modification of each such integral scheme.
items.strategy: Source: Stacks 42.29-42.35. Composition commutes with each of the three operations by applying the relevant axiom first to its inner and then its outer factor; restriction merely changes the indexing family. Proper pushforward gives the same property by cartesian push-pull and the divisor projection formula. Flat pullback does so by flat composition and cartesian push-pull. For divisor Gysin, proper/flat compatibility is checked on integral cycles using the order/length definition when the cycle is not contained in the divisor, and $c_1(L)$ when it is; two Cartier Gysins commute. To verify the last assertion, when neither divisor contains the cycle their two cuts agree away from their common codimension-two locus, and the discrepancy at that locus is the principal-divisor boundary of the tame symbol $(-1)^{\operatorname{ord}a\operatorname{ord}b}a^{\operatorname{ord}b}/b^{\operatorname{ord}a}$; the one-dimensional order-function key lemma proves its divisor zero in the Chow quotient. When a cycle is contained in one divisor, the operation is $c_1$ of that line bundle and commutation reduces to commutation of two first Chern operations, proved by the same rational-section argument. This supplies the Cartier axiom without higher Gysin. For the equality criterion, every cycle is a finite sum of pushforwards of integral fundamental classes; commute $c$ with these pushforwards. If $h:V'\to V$ is proper birational and integral, $h_*[V']=[V]$, so equality on $[V']$ pushes to equality on $[V]$. This is a descent test for operations, not an assertion that Chow pullback to the modification is injective.

items.title: Operational Chern classes, Whitney formula and regular sections
items.statement: Every rank-$r$ vector bundle $E$ on a finite type scheme $T$ has operators $c_j(E):A_m(T')\to A_{m-j}(T')$ for every $T'\to T$, defined by the projective bundle relation and commuting with the bivariant operations. They satisfy $c_0=1$, $c_j=0$ for $j>r$, $c(L)=1+c_1(L)$, arbitrary base restriction, $c(E)=c(E')c(E'')$ for $0\to E'\to E\to E''\to0$, and a splitting principle by iterated projective bundles whose flat pullback is injective after every base change. If a section of $E$ on a pure $n$ dimensional scheme $T$ has zero scheme regularly embedded of codimension $r$, then $c_r(E)\cap[T]=[Z(s)]$ in $A_{n-r}(T)$. These are operators on singular schemes; a Chow ring is not required.
items.strategy:
Sources: Stacks 42.37-42.44. For every base $T'$ and cycle $\alpha$, use the unique projective bundle expansion to define $c_j(E)\cap\alpha$ by $\sum_{j=0}^r(-1)^j\xi^{r-j}\cap\pi^*(c_j(E)\cap\alpha)=0$. All terms have the same dimension; uniqueness follows from the basis and existence by expanding $\xi^r\pi^*\alpha$. Commuting any proper, flat or divisor operation through this equation and cancelling the basis proves the corresponding compatibility. More generally for any bivariant operation $b$ the projective bundle square and $b\xi=\xi b$ give $b c_j(E)=c_j(E)b$. A line bundle gives $\xi=c_1(L)$.
For Whitney, first if $0\to1\to E\to F\to0$, $\mathbb P(F)\subset\mathbb P(E)$ is the divisor of the induced section of $\mathcal O(1)$. Push its defining degree-$r-1$ relation to $\mathbb P(E)$: this gives the degree-$r$ relation with coefficients $c_j(F)$ and last coefficient zero. Uniqueness gives $c(E)=c(F)$. For a line subbundle $L$, twist by $L^{-1}$. The identity $\mathbb P(E\otimes L^{-1})=\mathbb P(E)$ shifts $\xi$ to $\xi-c_1(L)$; expanding its powers by the binomial formula transforms the relations into $c_j(E)=c_j(F)+c_1(L)c_{j-1}(F)$. This is uniquely forced degree by degree because the coefficient of $c_j(E)$ is one. For higher-rank subbundle $E'$, pull to $\mathbb P(E')$ with kernel $H$ and line quotient $L$; set $Q=\pi^*E/H$, which is an extension of $\pi^*E''$ by $L$. Induction gives $c(\pi^*E)=c(H)c(Q)=c(H)c(L)c(\pi^*E'')=c(\pi^*E')c(\pi^*E'')$; injectivity of projective bundle pullback descends the identity. Iterating kernels yields filtrations by lines; this construction applies to a finite family simultaneously and remains injective after any base change. This proves the splitting principle after Whitney, with no circular deduction from a filtration whose additivity has not yet been proved.
For the section formula use induction on $r$, the Cartier case being $r=1$. On $\mathbb P(E)$ let $t$ be the image of $s$ in $\mathcal O(1)$ and $H$ the kernel of $\pi^*E\to\mathcal O(1)$. On $Z(t)$ the section lifts to $H$ with zero scheme $\pi^{-1}Z(s)$. At its generic points the original regular sequence is transformed by an invertible change of generators to $t$ and $r-1$ generators, so they remain regular. The divisor $Z(t)$ has dimension $n+r-2$ and is generically Cartier: away from a whole projective fibre its equation is a nonzero linear polynomial; a whole fibre could be generic in this dimension only over a point of $Z(s)$ of dimension $n-1$, impossible since $\dim Z(s)=n-r$ and $r>1$. Thus the Cartier section formula and induction give $c_r(\pi^*E)[\mathbb P(E)]=c_{r-1}(H)[Z(t)]=[\pi^{-1}Z(s)]$. Injective $\pi^*$ gives the result.

items.title: Homotopy invariance for a vector bundle
items.statement: For any rank-$r$ vector bundle $p:E\to T$, flat pullback $p^*:A_m(T)\to A_{m+r}(E)$ is bijective, including after every base change. Its inverse is denoted $s_E^!$.
items.strategy: Stacks 42.36.3. Compactify $E$ using the quotient-convention bundle $q:\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1)\to T$. The infinity divisor is $j:\mathbb P(E^\vee)\to\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1)$, with divisor class $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ from the trivial summand; its complement is $E$. Localization gives $A_*(\mathbb P(E^\vee))\xrightarrow{j_*}A_*(\mathbb P(E^\vee\oplus1))\to A_*(E)\to0$. The projective bundle basis on the source has $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^{r-1}$, and on the target $1,\xi,\ldots,\xi^r$. Cartier cutting gives $j_*\pi^*\alpha=\xi q^*\alpha$ for every cycle (both sides are the zero of the trivial-summand section on the pulled-back cycle). By the $c_1$ projection formula, $j_*(\xi^a\pi^*\alpha)=\xi^{a+1}q^*\alpha$. Therefore the image of $j_*$ is precisely the positive-$\xi$ summands, leaving the $q^*$ summand as quotient. Restriction of $q^*$ is $p^*$, proving the isomorphism and its grading. This computation applies verbatim after any base change, since both bundles and their bases pull back.

items.title: Koszul resolutions and restriction to deformation fibres
items.statement: A section $s$ of a rank-$d$ bundle $Q$ whose zero scheme is cut out locally by a regular sequence has exact Koszul resolution $\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$. Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth quasi-projective varieties, the strict transform $F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from $B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to $P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.
items.strategy:
Koszul exactness follows by induction on the regular sequence: the complex on $(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ is the mapping cone of multiplication by $a_d$ on the complex on $(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})$. Its long exact homology sequence leaves only degree zero because $a_d$ is injective on $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})$, with quotient $A/(a_1,\ldots,a_d)$. Exterior powers and contraction by $s$ are canonical under change of local frames, so these local resolutions glue. For fibre restriction, the two-term free resolution $[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O]$ of $\mathcal O/(t)$ shows that $\operatorname{Tor}_1(H,\mathcal O/(t))=\ker(t:H\to H)=0$ and all higher Tors vanish. Therefore derived tensor of any locally free resolution has homology only $H/tH$, proving ordinary restriction is exact. One must check $H$, not merely the ambient scheme, is flat or $t$-torsion-free.
For the smooth deformation, étale locally on $Y$, the embedding is given by coordinate regular sequence $a_1,\ldots,a_d$. The blowup charts of $(a_1,\ldots,a_d,t)$ are smooth: the $t$-chart has coordinates $u_j=a_j/t,t$ plus coordinates on $X$, and the $a_j$-charts have the ratios $a_l/a_j,t/a_j$ plus $a_j$ and the remaining smooth coordinates. This follows by base change from the corresponding affine-space charts, using the local smooth conormal sequence to choose étale coordinates. Thus $M$ is smooth, quasi-projective and has finite locally free coherent resolutions by the named K-theory supplier. The strict transform of $X\times\mathbb P^1$ is isomorphic to that scheme (its centre is its Cartier infinity divisor); at infinity it lies entirely in the $t$-chart, at $u_1=\cdots=u_d=0$. It meets $P$ at the section $[0:1]$ and misses $B$, which meets $P$ in $\mathbb P(N)$. On this chart $P$ has equation $t$, which acts injectively on $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ since that sheaf is the vector bundle on $X\times\mathbb P^1$. The ordinary fibre equation is likewise injective. The restriction lemma proves exactness on $P$ and on $Y$. Since the sheaf is zero near $B$, its resolution restricts to an exact complex there: locally an exact bounded complex of vector bundles resolving zero is split exact, by induction starting at its last cokernel. These calculations fill the flatness and component restriction omissions in Vakil19.

items.title: Zero-section Gysin and the excess vector subbundle formula
items.statement: For a rank-$r$ vector bundle $p:N\to T$, let $s_N^!=(p^*)^{-1}$. If $0\to N'\to N\to Q\to0$ is exact and $a:N'\hookrightarrow N$ is the vector subbundle immersion, then $s_N^!a_*p'^*\alpha=c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(Q)\cap\alpha$. In particular $s_N^!s_*\alpha=c_r(N)\cap\alpha$. These identities and proper/flat/divisor compatibility hold after every base change.
items.strategy: Sources: Stacks 42.44.2 and 42.36.3. Proper, flat and divisor compatibility of $s_N^!$ follows by applying the bijection $p^*$ and the corresponding push-pull or Cartier identity to each desired equality. The universal section of $p^*Q$ on $N$ is the image of its vector coordinate under $N\to Q$; its zero scheme is $N'$. For every integral $V\subset T$, its inverse image in $N$ is integral; this section cuts a polynomial regular sequence of $\operatorname{rank}Q$ fibre coordinates after a local splitting of the bundle sequence, so the regular-section formula gives $a_*p'^*[V]=c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(p^*Q)p^*[V]=p^*(c_{\operatorname{rank}Q}(Q)[V])$. Linearity and bijective $p^*$ prove the displayed equality. Put $N'=0$ to obtain the zero-section/self-intersection formula. All splittings here are local and used to verify regularity only, not to assert a global bundle splitting.

items.title: Specialization as a bivariant operation and base change
items.statement: For a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow T$ with a surjection $N^\vee\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ from a rank-$d$ bundle on $Z$, each $T'\to T$ gives $Z'=Z\times_TT'$, a closed cone embedding $a:C_{Z'}T'\hookrightarrow N'=N|_{Z'}$, and an operation $c(Z,T,N):=(p'^*)^{-1}a_*\sigma_{Z'/T'}:A_m(T')\to A_{m-d}(Z')$. This family is bivariant and compatible with arbitrary base restriction. If $N'_{0}\subset N'$ is a vector subbundle through which the cone embedding factors, replacing $N'$ by $N'_{0}$ multiplies the operation by the top Chern operator of $N'/N'_{0}$.
items.strategy: Sources: Stacks 42.48.1-48.3 and 42.54.1-54.5, all read. The ideal generating $Z'$ is $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$, so its powers are generated by the images of powers of $\mathcal I$; hence $\operatorname{Sym}(N'^\vee)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}}\mathcal O_{T'}$. This proves the cone embedding for arbitrary, including nonflat, base change. For a proper $W\to\mathbb P^1_T$ isomorphic over $\mathbb A^1_T$, define infinity specialization on each base by lifting $\mathbb A^1$ pullback and applying Cartier Gysin at infinity. Localization and the trivial fibre normal line make the lift irrelevant. To commute it with a proper map, push forward any lift; its restriction is the proper push of the original pullback, and Cartier Gysin commutes with pushforward. To commute with flat pullback, pull back the lift and use flat/Cartier compatibility. To commute with a Cartier divisor Gysin, apply that Gysin to the lift and use commutation of Cartier Gysins; its ordinary restriction is the lift of the desired input. These arguments prove each bivariant axiom without an unspecified diagram chase. If a proper $W_1\to W_2$ is an isomorphism over the ordinary part, pushing a lift from $W_1$ to $W_2$ proves equality of their infinity operations after pushforward. Under nonflat base change, the blowup of $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{T'}$ has a closed immersion into the base change of the original blowup, induced by the surjection of Rees algebras, and is an isomorphism over the ordinary part. The preceding proper comparison therefore shows that the cone portions give the same class after pushforward to $N'$. Proper pushforward, open restriction and $(p'^*)^{-1}$ are bivariant, proving the claim. If the cone factors through $N'_0$, apply the vector subbundle identity of [[lem-zero-section-gysin-and-excess-vector-subbundle]] to its specialization class (write that class as $p_0^*\beta$ by homotopy invariance). This gives the excess factor exactly.

items.title: Commutation and composition of refined Gysin operations
items.statement: The operations $c(Z,T,N)$ of [[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]] commute with every bivariant operation. Given $Z\subset Y\subset T$ and virtual normal bundles fitting into $0\to N_{Y/T}|_Z\to N_{Z/T}\to N_{Z/Y}\to0$ compatible with the conormal maps, $c(Z,T,N_{Z/T})=c(Z,Y,N_{Z/Y})c(Y,T,N_{Y/T})$. For regular embeddings this yields $(j i)^!=i^!j^!$, after all base changes. If a regular embedding is followed by a smooth projection, its Gysin likewise composes with the projection pullback; in particular a regular section of a smooth morphism gives $s^!p^*=1$.
items.strategy:
Sources: Stacks 42.54.8-54.10 and 42.59.1-59.6. Test equality on integral $T'\to T$, allowing proper birational modification by the bivariant criterion. If its inverse image of $Z$ is all of $T'$, the cone is the zero section and $c$ is the top Chern operator by [[lem-zero-section-gysin-and-excess-vector-subbundle]], hence central. Otherwise blow up the nonzero ideal of the inverse image of $Z$. The new inverse image is an effective Cartier divisor; the pulled-back virtual normal bundle surjects onto its normal line and the kernel is a vector bundle $Q$ (dually the conormal surjection has locally free kernel). The excess formula gives $c=c_{\mathrm{top}}(Q)D^!$. Both factors commute with every bivariant operation, respectively by [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] and the Cartier axiom. Proper pushforward of the fundamental class proves commutation on the original integral base. Thus no unproved Gysin commutation is used.
For composition, use the same equality criterion and blow up the product of the two nonzero ideals to make both inverse images Cartier; invertibility of a product ideal implies invertibility of its factors locally on this blowup, since each factor generates an invertible fractional ideal. If an inverse image is the entire base, the identity reduces directly to the excess vector subbundle formula. In the Cartier case split off the excess bundle for $Y/T$ using the two exact sequences. Centrality of its top Chern operation reduces the question to the case that $N_{Y/T}$ is the normal line to $Y$ in $T$. Denote its zero section by $o:Y\to C_YT$. The essential cone identity is $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$ as a class in $A_{n-1}(C_ZT\times_{C_YT}Y)$ for integral $T$ of dimension $n$. Here is its local justification, filling the calculation omitted in Stacks54.9: if the Cartier ideals are $(a)$ for $Z$ and $(b)$ for $Y$, the inclusion $Z\subset Y$ gives $b=ac$. The open deformation ring for $Z$ is $A[t,a/t]\subset A[t,t^{-1}]$, and the ring for $Y$ maps to it by $b/t\mapsto c(a/t)$. Hence there is a morphism of open deformation spaces, including their special cones. The strict transform of $Y\times\mathbb P^1$ in the $Z$ blowup is the blowup of $Y\times\mathbb P^1$ in $Z\times\{\infty\}$: on affine charts this is the quotient by the saturation of $(b)$ with respect to the exceptional equation. Its cone part at infinity is therefore $C_ZY$. The Cartier divisor on the $Y$ deformation given by its vertex section restricts on the ordinary part to $Y\subset T$; its pullback cut of the $Z$ deformation agrees there with the strict transform. Differences are supported at infinity, so infinity Gysin kills them. Cartier commutation now gives $o^![C_ZT]=[C_ZY]$. This also treats the component contained in the divisor using the Cartier $c_1$ rule, rather than treating $cu=0$ as always a regular equation. In the vector-bundle square $N_{Z/Y}\subset N_{Z/T}\to N_{Y/T}|_Z$, Cartier Gysin for the kernel commutes with bundle pullback and sends the first cone class to the second by this identity. Apply the two inverse bundle pullbacks: they characterize precisely the two sides of the composition formula, so they agree. Push down the modifications to finish.
Finally, for a regular immersion $s:Z\hookrightarrow P$ with $P\to T$ smooth and $Z\to T$ flat of the expected dimension, each flat pullback of an integral $[V]$ has normal cone to $Z\times_TV$ equal to the normal bundle of $s$ restricted there. Locally the regular equations remain a regular sequence on this pullback: smooth coordinates and flatness of $Z/T$ imply Tor independence, by the local flatness criterion. Specialization gives its full normal bundle fundamental cycle; inverse bundle pullback gives $[Z\times_TV]$. This proves $s^!p^*=(ps)^*$, including the section case $ps=1$. Factor two graph presentations through their product over the base and apply the established immersion composition and this smooth identity; it proves independence and composition of graph Gysin for morphisms between smooth schemes. All normal-bundle equalities used in this argument are exact sequences, not global splittings.

items.title: Refined Gysin pullback for a regular embedding of smooth schemes
items.statement:
Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a regular closed embedding of codimension $d$ with normal bundle $N$. In particular a closed embedding of smooth schemes of constant codimension is regular. For any $f:Y'\to Y$, put $X'=X\times_YY'$ and $N'=N|_{X'}$. The pulled-back ideal gives a closed immersion $a:C_{X'}Y'\hookrightarrow N'$. Define
$$i^!_{Y'}=(p'^*)^{-1}a_*\sigma_{X'/Y'}:A_m(Y')\longrightarrow A_{m-d}(X'),$$
using [[def-deformation-to-the-normal-cone-and-specialization]] and [[lem-vector-bundle-chow-homotopy-invariance]]. No fibre product of deformation spaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with a fictitious map to $Y$ is used. The same construction for a regular locally closed embedding uses restriction to an open in which it is closed; the operations agree under further restriction and extension of cycles, so this is intrinsic.
For $h:Y''\to Y'$ and $h_X:X''=X\times_YY''\to X'$, properness of $h$ gives $i^!_{Y'}h_*=(h_X)_*i^!_{Y''}$, and flatness of $h$ gives $i^!_{Y''}h^*=h_X^*i^!_{Y'}$. These do not require the base-changed embedding to be regular. If $X'\hookrightarrow Y'$ is regular with normal bundle $N_0\subset N'$ and excess bundle $Q=N'/N_0$, then $i^!_{Y'}=c_{d-\operatorname{rank}N_0}(Q)\cap (i')^!$. In particular $i^!i_*\alpha=c_d(N)\cap\alpha$. Here $c_j$ means the already defined operational Chern operator of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]]; it later becomes the Chow-ring Chern class on a smooth scheme. Codimension-one Gysin equals Cartier divisor Gysin; refined Gysins commute, and $(ji)^!=i^!j^!$ for composed regular embeddings. They commute with Chern cap operations. After the smooth Chow ring is defined, $i_*(i^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot i_*\beta$ for $\alpha\in A^*(Y)$ and $\beta\in A^*(X)$, where $i^*$ is this Gysin under codimension grading.
items.strategy:
The construction and arbitrary-base-change bivariant axioms are proved in [[lem-gysin-specialization-bivariant-and-base-change]], with its excess vector subbundle formula. Self-intersection applies that formula to the base change $Y'=X$: the ideal is zero, its cone is the zero section, and the quotient bundle is $N$; use proper compatibility to identify this restricted operation with $i^!i_*$. For Cartier agreement, test on an integral base cycle. If it is not contained in the divisor, its cone is the normal line and the operation is its Cartier fundamental cycle; if contained, the zero-cone computation gives $c_1$ of the restricted normal line. These are exactly the two cases of Cartier Gysin. Commutation and composition, including the necessary cone calculation, are [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]. Locality for locally closed embeddings follows from the same cone formula on every cycle and independence of a lift in specialization; in each overlap the identical ideal and normal bundle give identical operators. The final product formula is read through the bivariant identification of the smooth Chow ring proved in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]; that is a later consequence rather than a prerequisite for this definition. Source route is Stacks42.48/53/54/59 with the exact local helpers above. Vakil16-17 supply construction and statements, but their omitted proofs do not establish these properties; Fulton has not been read and is not a proof premise.
Source status correction: Fulton was not retrieved/read and is a bibliographical comparison only. The proof prerequisites are the explicit local arguments and retrieved Stacks/Borel-Serre sources; any Vakil statement marked proof omitted is not accepted as proof evidence.

items.title: The intersection product and Chow ring of a smooth scheme
items.statement: For a smooth equidimensional finite type $k$-scheme $X$ of dimension $n$, $A^p(X)=A_{n-p}(X)$ is a commutative graded ring with unit $[X]$ and product $\alpha\beta=\Delta_X^!(\alpha\times\beta)$. The diagonal is a regular immersion (closed if $X$ is separated); use the locally closed extension of [[def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings]] otherwise. Exterior product on integral cycles is the fundamental cycle $[V\times_k W]$, with generic lengths and all components; over a non-algebraically-closed field this product scheme need not be integral. Exterior product descends to rational equivalence and is associative and symmetric. Every morphism $f:X'\to X$ of smooth schemes has a codimension-preserving ring pullback $f^*:=\Gamma_f^!\operatorname{pr}_X^*$; it agrees with flat pullback when $f$ is flat and obeys composition. For a proper such morphism, $f_*:A^p(X')\to A^{p+\dim X-\dim X'}(X)$ satisfies $f_*(f^*\alpha\,\beta)=\alpha f_*\beta$. Operational $c_j(E)$ correspond to classes $c_j(E)\cap[X]$ and their cap action is multiplication by these classes; in particular $c_1(L)\alpha=c_1(L)\cap\alpha$. More generally the operational action on $A_*(X)$ agrees with the product after the dimension identification.
items.strategy:
Sources: Stacks42.60-42.62. Fix integral $V\subset X$. Its exterior-product operation is proper pushforward of flat pullback along $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is therefore bivariant and factors through rational equivalence in the other input. Symmetry proves descent in the first input too. Associativity is checked on the fundamental cycles of triple products: the iterated flat pullbacks both give their generic lengths, by associativity of tensor products and flat length multiplicity; extension is bilinear. Such exterior-product operations commute with all bivariant operations because their two constituents do. Consequently associativity of $\Delta^!$ product follows by comparing the two embeddings $\Delta_{12},\Delta_{23}$ in $X^3$: their iterated Gysins both give the small diagonal Gysin by [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]], while exterior-product compatibility moves each inner Gysin into $X^3$. Symmetry of $\Delta$ gives ordinary commutativity (no cohomological sign).
For the unit, $\alpha\times[X]$ is the pullback of $\alpha$ by the smooth first projection, and $\Delta^!\operatorname{pr}_1^*=1$ by the smooth-section identity in that helper. Thus $\Delta^!(\alpha\times[X])=\alpha$ on every class, not merely on a generic open.
The full operational identification can be proved explicitly. A bivariant class $c\in A^p(X\to X)$ maps to $c[X]\in A_{n-p}(X)$. Conversely $\alpha\in A_{n-p}(X)$ assigns to $T\to X$ the operation $\beta\mapsto\Delta^!(\alpha\times\beta)$ on $T$; its proper, flat and Cartier compatibility comes from exterior product and refined Gysin. This operation evaluated on $[X]$ is $\alpha$ by the unit computation. To prove the inverse in the other direction, commute $c$ past the exterior product and diagonal Gysin: $\Delta^!((c[X])\times\beta)=c\Delta^!([X]\times\beta)=c\beta$. Hence composition of operational classes is exactly the product. For a graph, its immersion is regular since it is a section of a smooth projection; the graph Gysin constructed in the helper composes, is central, sends $[X]$ to $[X']$, and agrees with flat pullback by its smooth/flat composition identity. Thus applying graph Gysin to $c[X]$ gives the restricted operation $c[X']$, proving ring naturality and the unit assertion. For proper $f$, write $\alpha=c[X]$. Then $f_*(f^*\alpha\,\beta)=f_*(c\beta)=c f_*\beta=\alpha f_*\beta$ by the proper axiom. The operational Chern identification follows from the same isomorphism. This proves every displayed operation integrally and avoids relying on the rational Chern-character isomorphism.

items.title: Naturality and projection formula for the Chow ring
items.statement: For every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth equidimensional finite type schemes over $k$, $f^*:A^*(Y)\to A^*(X)$ is the graph Gysin pullback, preserves codimension and the unit, is a ring homomorphism, and obeys $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$. If $f$ is flat it is precisely the previously defined flat pullback. For proper $f$, proper pushforward shifts codimension by $\dim Y-\dim X$, obeys $(gf)_*=g_*f_*$ for proper composites, and $f_*(f^*\alpha\cdot\beta)=\alpha\cdot f_*\beta$. Flat/proper composition laws are asserted under their respective hypotheses, not by identifying the two kinds of operation.
items.strategy: Use the operational isomorphism and graph computation established in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]. Restriction of operational classes is a ring map and composes, so graph pullback is a unital ring map. For flat $f$, the graph's Gysin followed by the smooth projection is the flat pullback by [[lem-refined-gysin-commutation-and-composition]]. If $\alpha=c[Y]$, its pullback is $c[X]$ and the proper axiom gives $f_*(c\beta)=c f_*\beta$, the required projection formula. Proper composition is checked on each integral cycle using multiplication of generic degrees, with zero pushforward when dimension drops, and then descends to Chow groups. The degree shift follows from $A^p(X)=A_{\dim X-p}(X)$ and dimension preservation by proper pushforward of nonzero cycles. No undefined pullback for merely proper maps is used.

items.title: Chern classes of a vector bundle in the Chow ring
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a smooth equidimensional scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension $n$ ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]]), with Chow ring $A^*(X)$ ([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]). Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of rank $r\ge1$ ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]), with projective bundle $\pi:\mathbb P(\mathcal E)\to X$ and $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ ([[thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups]]).

**Definition.** By the projective bundle formula, $\xi^r\in A^r(\mathbb P(\mathcal E))$ has a unique expression
$$\xi^r+\sum_{i=1}^{r}(-1)^i c_i(\mathcal E)\,\xi^{r-i}=0\qquad\text{in }A^*(\mathbb P(\mathcal E)),$$
with $c_i(\mathcal E)\in A^i(X)$ pulled back from $X$; the classes $c_i(\mathcal E)$ are the **Chern classes** of $\mathcal E$. Set $c_0(\mathcal E):=1\in A^0(X)$, $c_i(\mathcal E):=0$ for $i>r$, and call $c(\mathcal E):=1+c_1(\mathcal E)+\dots+c_r(\mathcal E)$ the **total Chern class**.

**Basic properties.** (i) (Normalization) For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$: $c(\mathcal L)=1+c_1(\mathcal L)$ with $c_1(\mathcal L)\in A^1(X)$ the first Chern class of [[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]]; in particular $c_1(\mathcal O_X(D))=[D]$ for an effective Cartier divisor $D$. (ii) (Naturality) For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ of smooth equidimensional $k$-schemes, $c_i(f^*\mathcal E)=f^*c_i(\mathcal E)$. (iii) (Vanishing) $c_i(\mathcal E)=0$ for $i>\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E$ and $c_i(\mathcal E)\in A^i(X)$. (iv) (Direct sums of line bundles) If $\mathcal E\cong\mathcal L_1\oplus\dots\oplus\mathcal L_r$ then $c(\mathcal E)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1+c_1(\mathcal L_i))$. (v) (Top class) $c_r(\mathcal E)\cap[X]=[Z(s)]$ for a regular section $s$ of $\mathcal E$ with $\dim Z(s)=n-r$; in particular $c_r(\mathcal E)$ is the class of the zero locus of a regular section.
items.strategy: Define the classes by applying the operators of [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] to $[X]$ and use the operational-ring isomorphism in [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]. Its projective bundle relation gives exactly the displayed relation and uniqueness. Normalization, arbitrary morphism naturality, rank vanishing, Whitney and the line-summand formula are already established for the operators; restriction under the operational isomorphism is the graph pullback, so these become the claimed ring identities. The regular-section formula follows from the supplier's projective-bundle induction and gives its zero-scheme fundamental cycle, with generic multiplicities. No assertion that arbitrary $f^*$ is injective is used; only flag/projective bundle pullback is injective.

items.title: Additivity, naturality and the splitting principle for Chern classes
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type, and let $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Then:

1. (Whitney additivity) $c(\mathcal E)=c(\mathcal E')\,c(\mathcal E'')$ in the Chow ring $A^*(X)$ ([[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]], [[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]).
2. (Naturality) If $f:X'\to X$ is a flat morphism of smooth equidimensional $k$-schemes, then $c_i(f^*\mathcal E)=f^*c_i(\mathcal E)$ for all $i$.
3. (Splitting principle) There exists a morphism $f:X'\to X$, a composition of projective bundles (flag bundles) over $X$, such that $f^*:A^*(X)\to A^*(X')$ is injective and $f^*\mathcal E$ admits a filtration
$$0=\mathcal E_0\subseteq\mathcal E_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal E_r=f^*\mathcal E$$
with successive quotients invertible sheaves $\mathcal L_1,\dots,\mathcal L_r$; consequently $f^*c(\mathcal E)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1+c_1(\mathcal L_i))$. Any polynomial identity among Chern classes that is proved after replacing $\mathcal E$ by such a filtered bundle and $c_i(\mathcal E)$ by the elementary symmetric functions $e_i(c_1(\mathcal L_j))$ holds for $\mathcal E$ itself.
4. (Consequences) $c_i(\mathcal E^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(\mathcal E)$; $c_1(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=c_1(\mathcal L)+c_1(\mathcal M)$ for invertible sheaves; $c_i(\mathcal E)=0$ for $i>\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal E)$; and for an exact sequence of vector bundles the total Chern classes multiply (this is (1)).
items.strategy: Apply [[lem-operational-chern-classes-and-whitney-formula]] through the operational isomorphism of the smooth Chow ring. That supplier proves Whitney first by the line-subbundle and rank induction argument, then constructs flags by taking successive kernels of tautological line quotients, rather than assuming the kernel on $\mathbb P(E)$ is pulled from $X$. Each bundle pullback is injective by the projective bundle formula, so their composition is injective. A filtration gives the line-product formula by already proved Whitney. The dual filtration has quotients $L_j^{-1}$, whose first Chern operators are the negatives of those of $L_j$ by the rational-section divisor construction; multiplying $\prod(1-x_j)$ gives $c_i(E^\vee)=(-1)^ic_i(E)$. The tensor identity for two lines follows by taking the product of rational sections and adding their Cartier divisors. All vanishings are in the defining operator relation. This is the exact Stacks42.39-43 proof route with its local induction supplied.

items.title: Chern character and Todd class
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]), with Chow ring $A^*(X)$ ([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]) and $K(X):=K_0(X)=K^0(X)$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]], [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]). Write $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}:=A^*(X)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$.

**Chern roots.** The **Chern roots** of a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal E$ of rank $r$ are formal symbols $x_1,\dots,x_r$ with the property that the elementary symmetric functions in the $x_i$ are the Chern classes: $e_i(x_1,\dots,x_r)=c_i(\mathcal E)$ ([[def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle]]); by the splitting principle every symmetric polynomial expression in the $x_i$ with rational coefficients defines a well-defined element of $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ ([[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]).

**Chern character.** Define
$$\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E):=\sum_{j=1}^{r}e^{x_j}=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{1}{m!}\,p_m(c_1,\dots,c_m)\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where the second expression expands the power sums in the Chern classes; explicitly $\operatorname{ch}=r+c_1+\tfrac12(c_1^2-2c_2)+\tfrac16(c_1^3-3c_1c_2+3c_3)+\cdots$ (the denominators are why we tensor with $\mathbb Q$).

**Todd class.** Define
$$\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E):=\prod_{j=1}^{r}\frac{x_j}{1-e^{-x_j}}\in A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q};$$
explicitly $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=1+\tfrac12c_1+\tfrac1{12}(c_1^2+c_2)+\tfrac1{24}c_1c_2+\cdots$. For a smooth $X$ the **Todd class of $X$** is $\operatorname{td}(T_X)$ for the tangent bundle $T_X=\operatorname{Hom}(\Omega^1_{X/k},\mathcal O_X)$ ([[def-sheaf-relative-differentials]], [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]]).

**Line bundles.** For an invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ with $x=c_1(\mathcal L)$: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L)=e^{x}$ and $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=x/(1-e^{-x})=1+\tfrac12x+\tfrac1{12}x^2-\cdots$.
items.strategy:
Definitions via Chern roots, following Stacks, *Chow Homology*, Section 42.45 (tag 02UM, the Chern character and tensor products) and Section 42.65 (tag 02UN, Todd classes), and Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 6 (Chern classes) and 7 (the Todd class $T(X)$ of the tangent bundle, an element of $A(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$); the explicit expansions are Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, 3.2.3 and Vakil 245 Class 18 Sections 2.1-2.2 (the definitions $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\sum e^{\alpha_i}$ and $\operatorname{td}(E)=\prod Q(\alpha_i)$, with $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$). Well-definedness of the expressions in the Chern classes is the splitting principle of [[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]: any two filtrations with invertible quotients give the same symmetric expression because symmetric polynomials in the roots are the Chern classes; rational coefficients are needed for the exponential and the geometric expansions. The tangent bundle is locally free of rank $\dim X$ by [[thm-differentials-smooth-locally-free]].
Source status correction: Fulton was not retrieved/read and is a bibliographical comparison only. The proof prerequisites are the explicit local arguments and retrieved Stacks/Borel-Serre sources; any Vakil statement marked proof omitted is not accepted as proof evidence.

items.title: Additivity of the Chern character and multiplicativity of the Todd class
items.statement:
In the setting of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]] let $0\to\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E''\to0$ be a short exact sequence of finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-modules ([[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]]). Then:

1. $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E')+\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E'')$ in $A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$; hence $\operatorname{ch}$ is additive in exact sequences and descends to a group homomorphism
$$\operatorname{ch}:K_0(X)\longrightarrow A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
2. $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E')\,\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E'')$; hence $\operatorname{td}$ is multiplicative in exact sequences and depends only on the class of $\mathcal E$ in $K_0(X)$.
3. For finite locally free $\mathcal E,\mathcal F$: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F)=\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)$, $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\vee)=\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)$ (with $x\mapsto-x$ convention: if $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\sum e^{x_j}$ then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E^\vee)=\sum e^{-x_j}$), and $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O_X)=\operatorname{rank}=1$. Hence $\operatorname{ch}:K_0(X)\to A^*(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ is a ring homomorphism (with the product on $K_0$ induced by tensor product).
4. For a flat morphism $f:X'\to X$ of smooth equidimensional $k$-schemes: $f^*\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{ch}(f^*\mathcal E)$ and $f^*\operatorname{td}(\mathcal E)=\operatorname{td}(f^*\mathcal E)$; and $\operatorname{td}(T_{X\times_kX'})=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cdot\operatorname{pr}_2^*\operatorname{td}(T_{X'})$.
5. For line bundles: $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal L_1\oplus\dots\oplus\mathcal L_r)=\sum e^{c_1(\mathcal L_j)}$ and $\operatorname{td}(\mathcal L)=\tfrac{c_1(\mathcal L)}{1-e^{-c_1(\mathcal L)}}$ (formal series); the terms of degree $>\dim X$ vanish.
items.strategy: Apply the splitting principle ([[lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting]]): after pulling back along the flag bundle $f:X'\to X$ the bundles acquire filtrations with invertible quotients $\mathcal L'_1,\dots$ and $\mathcal L''_1,\dots$, so $\operatorname{ch}(f^*\mathcal E)=\sum_{j}e^{c_1(\mathcal L_j)}$ with the roots running through the union of the roots of $\mathcal E'$ and $\mathcal E''$, giving additivity; injectivity of $f^*$ on the Chow ring concludes (1). Similarly the roots of $\mathcal E$ are those of $\mathcal E'$ together with those of $\mathcal E''$, and $Q(x)=x/(1-e^{-x})$ satisfies $Q(0)=1$, so the products interleave, giving (2). For (3), after splitting both bundles the roots of $\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal F$ are the pairwise sums $x_i+y_j$ and $e^{x_i+y_j}=e^{x_i}e^{y_j}$; duality negates the roots. Statements (4) and (5) are immediate from naturality of Chern classes and the definitions. References: Stacks, *Chow Homology*, Section 42.45 (tag 02UM) for the Chern character as an additive and multiplicative map, Section 42.65 (tag 02UN) for multiplicativity of the Todd class, and Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 2.1 (the two Exercises stated there).

items.title: Riemann-Roch for projections from projective space
items.statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $Y$ be a nonsingular equidimensional $k$-scheme of finite type ([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[cor-smooth-variety-classical-scheme-conventions-agree]]), let $n\ge0$ and let
$$p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\longrightarrow Y$$
be the projection. For every $\alpha\in K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)$ ([[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(p_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;p_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_{\mathbb P^n\times_kY})\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd classof [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $p_!$ is the K-theory pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]], [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]) and $p_*$ is the proper pushforward on Chow groups ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Equivalently, writing $\tau_X(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_X)$, the diagram
$$\begin{array}{ccc}K_0(\mathbb P^n\times_kY) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(\mathbb P^n\times_kY)_{\mathbb Q}\\ \downarrow p_! & & \downarrow p_*\\ K_0(Y) & \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } & A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\end{array}$$
commutes. The case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch for $\mathbb P^n$, and the case of a general projective-bundle projection is obtained by the same argument applied to the projective bundle formula.
items.strategy: Vakil 245 Class 19, first Theorem (``GRR is true for $\mathbb P^m\times Y\to Y$''), proof as written there: the naturality square $K(Y)\otimes K(\mathbb P^m)\to A(Y)_{\mathbb Q}\otimes A(\mathbb P^m)_{\mathbb Q}\to A(Y\times\mathbb P^m)_{\mathbb Q}$ commutes by (4) of [[lem-chern-character-and-todd-class-multiplicativity]] (the tangent bundle of a product is the direct sum of the pullbacks of the tangent bundles, so the Todd class multiplies), the top horizontal arrow is surjective by [[lem-k-theory-of-projective-space-and-projections]] (the cellular decomposition of $\mathbb P^m$), and the composite $K(Y)\otimes K(\mathbb P^m)\to K(Y\times\mathbb P^m)\xrightarrow{p_!}K(Y)$ is computed by the base case $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$: GRR for $\mathbb P^m\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is proved directly by the residue/coefficient computation $\sum_n(-1)^n\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal O(n))\,\operatorname{td}(\mathbb P^m)$ (Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 9, Proposition 10, computing $\chi(\mathbb P^m,\mathcal O(n))=\binom{n+m}{m}$ by a contour/residue identity; Vakil 245 Class 18 Section 5 for the same computation). Borel-Serre 9 Propositions 9-10 is the independent complete treatment of the same statement; their Corollary states ``R-R is true for the projection $A\times P\to A$''.

items.title: Riemann-Roch for a closed embedding of smooth varieties
items.statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ a closed immersion of nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective finite type $k$-varieties, with rank-$d$ normal bundle $N$. For $E\in K^0(X)=G_0(X)$,
$$\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)=i_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}\bigr)\quad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
Equivalently $\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)=i_*(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(T_X))$. The tangent relation is the exact sequence $0\to T_X\to i^*T_Y\to N\to0$, hence $[i^*T_Y]=[T_X]+[N]$ in $K^0(X)$; a splitting as bundles is neither asserted nor needed. The two $i_*$ symbols denote respectively coherent $K$ pushforward and Chow proper pushforward. A vector bundle on $X$ suffices to prove the formula, by finite resolution and additivity.
items.strategy:
Sources: Vakil19 §2 gives the deformation route but is a sketch in its Koszul step; Borel-Serre1958 §§10-16 independently proves the embedding theorem by the blowup/excess route. The following closes the deformation route locally.
Model case: write $P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{quot}}(N^\vee\oplus1)$, with projection $p$ and tautological sequence $0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to p^*(N\oplus1)\to Q\to0$. The image of $1$ in $Q$ is a section whose zero scheme is $s:X\hookrightarrow P$, the line $1$; in its affine $N$ chart it is precisely the regular sequence of $d$ vector coordinates, and $s^*Q=N$. The Koszul resolution of [[lem-koszul-resolution-and-flat-fibre-restriction]], tensored with $p^*E$, gives $\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)=\operatorname{ch}(p^*E)\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{ch}(\bigwedge^jQ^\vee)$, entirely in the ambient ring $A^*(P)_{\mathbb Q}$. After injective flag pullback, if $x_j$ are the roots of $Q$, the sum is $\prod_j(1-e^{-x_j})=c_d(Q)\operatorname{td}(Q)^{-1}$. The regular-section formula gives $c_d(Q)=s_*[X]$ and the ring projection formula gives $c_d(Q)\gamma=s_*(s^*\gamma)$ for every $\gamma\in A^*(P)$. Substituting $\gamma=\operatorname{td}(Q)^{-1}\operatorname{ch}(p^*E)$ proves $\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)=s_*(\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1}\operatorname{ch}(E))$. This corrects the wrongly typed $\operatorname{ch}(i^*E)$ ambient factor.
General case: take $M=\operatorname{Bl}_{X\times\{\infty\}}(Y\times\mathbb P^1)$, its proper projection $b:M\to Y$, and $F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$. Resolve $H=F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$ by a bounded complex $G_\bullet$ of vector bundles. Write $\gamma=\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{ch}(G_j)$, an operational class on $M$. The previous helper proves that on $j_0:Y\hookrightarrow M$, $G_\bullet$ resolves $i_*E$; on $k:P\hookrightarrow M$ it resolves $s_*E$; on $l:B\hookrightarrow M$ it is exact. The Cartier fibres at $0,\infty$ are linearly equivalent, hence $j_{0*}[Y]=k_*[P]+l_*[B]$ in $A_*(M)$, with multiplicity one since the centre is smooth. Capping with $\gamma$ and using the Chern projection formula gives
$ j_{0*}(\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)\cap[Y])=k_*(\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)\cap[P]) $;
the $B$ term is zero because its restricted complex is exact. Crucially push this equality by the proper $b$: $bj_0=1_Y$ and $bk=ip$, so $\operatorname{ch}(i_*E)\cap[Y]=i_*p_*\operatorname{ch}(s_*E)=i_*(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(N)^{-1})$. The final equality uses the model formula and $ps=1_X$. Thus no injectivity of $j_{0*}$ or informal equality of two fibre rings is assumed. Finite locally free resolution extends from vector bundles to all $K$ classes. Finally Whitney multiplicativity for the tangent exact sequence and the Chow projection formula give the equivalent Todd-tangent formula. Every use of deformation exactness and every pushforward is explicitly typed.

items.title: Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch for projective morphisms
items.statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective $k$-schemes of finite type ([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]], [[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]], [[def-proper-morphism]]); projectivity is exactly the hypothesis that $f$ factors as a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY$ followed by the projection $p:\mathbb P^n_k\times_kY\to Y$ for some $n\ge0$ ([[lem-projective-morphism-relative-proj-presentation]]). Then for every $\alpha\in K_0(X)$ (def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme, [[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]):
$$\operatorname{ch}\bigl(f_!(\alpha)\bigr)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\;=\;f_*\Bigl(\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\cdot\operatorname{td}(T_X)\Bigr)\qquad\text{in }A^*(Y)_{\mathbb Q},$$
where $\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{td}$ are the Chern character and Todd class of [[def-chern-character-and-todd-class]], $f_!$ is the $K$-theory pushforward ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]]) and $f_*$ is the proper Chow pushforward ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Equivalently $\tau_Y\circ f_!=f_*\circ\tau_X$ for $\tau_S(\alpha)=\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)\operatorname{td}(T_S)$. For $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$ this is Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch $\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\deg(\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal F)\operatorname{td}(T_X))$ ([[def-euler-characteristic-coherent-sheaf]]).
items.strategy: Factor $f=p\circ i$ with $i$ a closed immersion of smooth varieties and $p$ a projection from a projective bundle ([[lem-projective-morphism-relative-proj-presentation]]). Both factors satisfy Riemann-Roch: [[thm-rr-for-regular-embeddings]] for $i$ and [[thm-rr-for-projective-space-projections]] for $p$. The composition step is the elementary diagram chase recorded as Lemma 15(a) of Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, 7: the diagram $\tau$ commutes with $i_*$ and with $p_*$, so it commutes with $f_*=p_*i_*$; on the $K$-theory side one uses $(p\circ i)_!=p_!\circ i_!$ ([[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]](2)) and on the Chow side $(p\circ i)_*=p_*i_*$ ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]](2)). Vakil 245 Class 19 states and proves exactly this reduction (``the strategy is now to show GRR for $Y\times\mathbb P^m\to Y$ and for closed immersions'', and the composition Lemma). Borel-Serre 7 states the theorem in the same form for a proper morphism of nonsingular quasi-projective varieties over an algebraically closed field and proves the two special cases in Sections 9 and 15; their Proposition 15 is the injection case and their Corollary in Section 9 is the projection case. Hypotheses: $k$ algebraically closed (Borel-Serre, introduction); $X,Y$ nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective; $f$ projective (hence proper). The statement for arbitrary coherent $\alpha$ follows because $K_0$ is generated by vector bundles ([[lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves]]).

items.title: Conventions, hypotheses and scope of the Chow and Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch development
items.statement:
**Conventions.** (i) Rational equivalence is the version of [[def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence]] (Stacks 42.19.1, tag 02RW; Fulton 1.3), with order functions on possibly singular integral closed subschemes supplied by [[lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain]]; the equivalent $\mathbb P^1$-parametrized definition (Fulton 1.6; Stacks 43.8-43.9) is not used but is consistent with it. (ii) $A^*(X)$ always denotes the codimension-graded intersection ring of a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme ([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]]); for non-smooth schemes only $A_*(X)$ and $c_1\cap-$ are used, and products, Chern classes, Chern character and Todd class are only formed on smooth schemes. (iii) The intersection product is the diagonal Gysin construction (Stacks 42.62, tag 0FC0); the moving-lemma/Serre Tor-formula construction of Stacks Chapter 43 is an independent route to the same product for nonsingular projective varieties over an algebraically closed field and is not needed here.

**Hypotheses of the main theorem.** [[thm-grothendieck-riemann-roch-for-projective-morphisms]] is stated for an algebraically closed base field $k$, nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective $k$-schemes $X,Y$, and a projective (hence proper) morphism $f$; the field hypothesis is exactly the scope of the two independent complete treatments read for this scaffold (Borel-Serre, *Le theoreme de Riemann-Roch*, introduction and 7-16; Vakil 245 Classes 18-19). No claim is made here for singular targets, for proper non-projective morphisms, for pairs over a non-algebraically-closed field, or in the $K$-theory of perfect complexes; the singular and bivariant versions (Fulton, *Intersection Theory*, Chapters 18 and 17) are outside this pair.

**Choice.** The Axiom of Choice (and, where the coherence of higher direct images is invoked, Dependent Choice) is inherited from the published coherent-cohomology suppliers throughout; it is used to form the resolutions and direct images in [[def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory]] and is recorded in [[def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme]]. No choice-free claim is made stronger here. The definitional part of the Chow groups uses no choice beyond the free abelian group on a set.
items.strategy: Assembly of conventions, each clause tied to the item that establishes it: (i) rational equivalence is the order-function definition of def-chow-group-of-cycles-mod-rational-equivalence, with order functions on possibly singular integral subschemes supplied by lem-order-function-one-dimensional-local-domain; (ii) $A^*(X)$ denotes the codimension-graded intersection ring of a smooth equidimensional $k$-scheme (thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme), while for general schemes only $A_*(X)$ and the $c_1\cap-$ action are used; (iii) in K-theory, $K_0$ and $K^0$ are identified on regular schemes (def-grothendieck-group-of-coherent-sheaves-and-vector-bundles-on-a-scheme, lem-k-zero-vector-bundles-versus-coherent-sheaves) and pushforward is defined via higher direct images with the AC/DC inheritance declared (def-pushforward-in-algebraic-k-theory); (iv) the GRR statement proved on this page holds over an algebraically closed field for nonsingular irreducible quasi-projective varieties and projective morphisms (thm-grothendieck-riemann-roch-for-projective-morphisms), and the excluded cases (singular target, arbitrary field, non-projective proper morphisms, perfect-complex formulations, proper-intersection Tor formula) are listed with reasons. No new mathematics is asserted.

title: Chow Groups, Intersection Products, and Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch — Examples

items.title: The Chow ring of projective space
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$. In the Chow ring $A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)$ ([[thm-intersection-product-and-chow-ring-of-a-smooth-scheme]], [[lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space]]) put $h:=c_1(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n}(1))\in A^1(\mathbb P^n)$ ([[def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class]], [[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]). Then:

1. $A^d(\mathbb P^n_k)=\mathbb Z\cdot h^d$ for $0\le d\le n$ and $A^d(\mathbb P^n_k)=0$ for $d>n$; under the identification $A^d(X)=A_{n-d}(X)$ of the intersection product with the cycle groups, the class $h^d$ corresponds to the class $[\Lambda^{n-d}]$ of a linear subspace of codimension $d$: equivalently $h^d\cap[\mathbb P^n]=[\Lambda^{n-d}]$. In particular
$$A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)\;\cong\;\mathbb Z[h]/(h^{n+1}),$$
the isomorphism sending $h$ to $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$.
2. (Degrees of products) The degree isomorphism $\deg:A^n(\mathbb P^n_k)\to\mathbb Z$ of [[lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space]] satisfies $\deg(h^n)=1$. If $H_1,\dots,H_n\subseteq\mathbb P^n$ are reduced hypersurfaces of degrees $d_1,\dots,d_n$ ([[def-degree-projective-hypersurface]]) with $H_i=V(f_i)$ for nonconstant square-free forms $f_i$ of degree $d_i$, then $[H_i]=d_i\,h$ in $A^1(\mathbb P^n)$ and
$$[H_1]\cdot[H_2]\cdots[H_n]=(d_1d_2\cdots d_n)\,h^n,\qquad \deg\bigl([H_1]\cdots[H_n]\bigr)=d_1d_2\cdots d_n.$$

**Discussion.** This is the Chow-ring form of Bezout's theorem: the degree of the product of the hypersurface classes is the Bezout number. The identification of this product class with the cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection of the $H_i$, with its local intersection multiplicities, is the classical proper-intersection theorem and is not claimed here; for plane curves (n=2, curves without common components) the corresponding local-multiplicity statement is developed on the plane-curves page.
items.strategy: Compute, in order: (1) apply the projective bundle formula (thm-projective-bundle-formula-for-chow-groups) to the rank-$(n+1)$ free bundle on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, whose projectivization is $\mathbb P^n_k$, to get $A^*(\mathbb P^n_k)=\mathbb Z[\xi]/(\xi^{n+1})$ with $\xi=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; set $h:=\xi$. (2) Identify the generators with linear subspaces: by induction on $d$, intersecting with a hyperplane $H\not\supseteq\Lambda$ of complementary position, the cap-action formula $c_1(\mathcal O(1))\cap[V]=[V\cap H]$ of def-intersection-with-a-cartier-divisor-and-first-chern-class gives $h^d\cap[\mathbb P^n]=[\Lambda^{n-d}]$, so $A^d(\mathbb P^n)=\mathbb Z\cdot h^d$ corresponds to $A_{n-d}$; in particular $h^n=[\mathrm{pt}]$ with $\deg h^n=1$ (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space fixes the degree isomorphism on $A_0$). (3) For hypersurfaces $H_i$ of degrees $d_i$, the class is $[H_i]=d_i h$ (def-degree-projective-hypersurface with the normalisation and additivity of $c_1$ from def-chern-classes-of-a-vector-bundle and lem-chern-class-naturality-additivity-and-splitting), so $\deg([H_1]\cdots[H_n])=d_1\cdots d_n$. (4) State explicitly that this computes the product in the Chow ring; the identification with the cycle of the scheme-theoretic intersection is the proper-intersection/Tor-multiplicity statement, deliberately outside this page's scope.

items.title: Scheme-theoretic preimages do not define a pullback on Chow groups
items.statement:
**Statement refuted.** For every morphism $f:Y\to X$ of smooth projective $k$-varieties, the **scheme-theoretic preimage recipe** — send an integral closed subscheme $V\subseteq X$ to the cycle $[f^{-1}(V)]$ of its scheme-theoretic preimage ([[lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme]]) and extend the assignment linearly to all cycles — descends to a well-defined homomorphism of abelian groups $A_*(X)\to A_*(Y)$; that is, preimage cycles of rationally equivalent cycles are rationally equivalent.

**Counterexample.** Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the blowup and Proj suppliers. Let $k$ be a field, let $X=\mathbb P^2_k$, let $p\in\mathbb P^2(k)$ be a rational point and let $\pi:Y=\operatorname{Bl}_pX\to X$ be the blowup of $X$ at $p$, with exceptional curve $E=\pi^{-1}(p)$ ([[def-blowup-scheme-along-ideal]], [[def-exceptional-divisor-blowup]]). Then $E\cong\mathbb P^1_k$ and $Y$ is a smooth projective surface ([[thm-blowup-regular-surface-closed-point-regular]]), $\pi$ is proper ([[thm-blowup-projective]]) and birational ([[cor-blowup-birational-integral-scheme]]), and $\pi$ restricts to an isomorphism $\pi^{-1}(X\smallsetminus\{p\})\to X\smallsetminus\{p\}$ ([[lem-blowup-isomorphism-off-center]]).

Choose a rational point $q\ne p$. In $A_0(\mathbb P^2_k)\cong\mathbb Z$ the classes of $k$-rational points are determined by degree ([[lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space]]), so
$$[p]=[q]\qquad\text{in }A_0(\mathbb P^2_k).$$
On the other hand the preimage cycles are not even in the same degree: $\pi^{-1}(p)=E$ is a curve, giving $[E]\in Z_1(Y)$, whereas $\pi^{-1}(q)=\{q'\}$ is a single reduced point, giving $[q']\in Z_0(Y)$.

If the recipe descended to a homomorphism $\varphi:A_*(X)\to A_*(Y)$, then $[p]=[q]$ would force $[E]=[q']$ in $A_*(Y)$. Apply the proper pushforward $\pi_*$, which is well defined on rational equivalence ([[lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined]]). Since $\pi(E)=\{p\}$ has dimension $0<1=\dim E$, dimension reasons give $\pi_*[E]=0$; and since $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $q$, $\pi_*[q']=[q]$. Together with $[E]=[q']$ this would give $[q]=0$ in $A_0(\mathbb P^2_k)$, contradicting that $[q]$ has degree $1$.

Hence the preimage cycles of the rationally equivalent cycles $[p]$ and $[q]$ are not rationally equivalent, and the scheme-theoretic preimage recipe is not well defined on Chow groups.

**Discussion.** The obstruction is the jump of fibre dimension at $p$; for flat morphisms the recipe is the flat pullback of [[lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups]] and is well defined, while in general one needs the expected-dimension correction provided by the refined Gysin construction ([[def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings]], and the Gysin construction for complete-intersection morphisms beyond the scope of this page). The counterexample refutes only the preimage recipe: it makes no claim about whether some corrected operation can define a pullback for the morphism above.
items.strategy: Direct proof in four steps, all from scaffolded and published items. (1) Rational equivalence: $A_0(\mathbb P^2_k)\cong\mathbb Z$ is detected by degree (lem-chow-groups-of-projective-space), so the two $k$-rational points satisfy $[p]=[q]$; equivalently $[p]-[q]=\operatorname{div}(r)$ for the ratio $r$ of linear forms cutting the joining line. (2) Preimage cycles: $\pi^{-1}(p)=E\cong\mathbb P^1$ (thm-blowup-regular-surface-closed-point-regular, def-exceptional-divisor-blowup) and $\pi^{-1}(q)$ is the single reduced point $q'$ over $q\ne p$ (lem-blowup-isomorphism-off-center); the cycle of a preimage scheme is the corresponding basis class (lem-cycle-of-a-closed-subscheme). (3) Suppose the recipe were well defined on rational equivalence; then $[E]=[q']$ in $A_*(Y)$. The proper pushforward of lem-proper-pushforward-of-cycles-well-defined is well defined on rational equivalence and gives $\pi_*[E]=0$ (dimension drop $0<1$) and $\pi_*[q']=[q]$ (isomorphism over $q$, extension degree $1$), hence $[q]=0$, contradicting $\deg[q]=1$. (4) The hypotheses are sharp: pure fibre dimension fails exactly at $p$, so the flat case lem-flat-pullback-chow-groups does not apply, and the correct replacement is the refined Gysin construction of def-refined-gysin-pullback-for-regular-embeddings.
